articleTitle: Modeling of 2D ADI-FDTD for THz Region Using a Tridiagonal Matrix Inversion Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This study investigates a Transverse Electric (TE) mode using the 2D Alternating Direction Implicit (ADI) FDTD method. A 200×200 grid is designed with a PML boundary so that waves in the boundary don't reflect back or scatter outside of the grid. ADI-FDTD is an unconditionally stable method that isn't restricted by CFL conditions. We present a matrix inversion approach that uses the L U decomposition method to generate the implicit electric and magnetic field equations. Around 50–60 % of computation time reduction with small errors was observed with a 3THz electric wave. This time efficiency is dependent on the courant number (CN) and the effect of changing CN is discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Wearable MagnetoCardioGraphy (MCG) Sensor Using a Single Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We have previously reported a wearable magneto-cardiography (MCG) sensor that utilizes a coil array capable of detecting the weak magnetic fields generated by the heart. In this work, we improve upon our previous design by reducing the number of coils from seven (7) to one (1) while also achieving significantly better detection results. Experimental validation on a human subject shows an increase in heart beat detection accuracy from 28.4% to 96.8%. Key to this improved performance is a new signal processing method that significantly reduces noise. Given the increasing importance of MCG as a reliable and non-contact method of assessing cardiac health and cognitive workload, the proposed sensor is expected to have significant clinical impact.

articleTitle: Integral Equation-Based Topology Optimization of an EMI Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Topology Optimization (TO) stands as a powerful instrument for elevating the design paradigm of electromagnetic devices, particularly with the integration of advanced additive manufacturing methodologies. Through the coupling of the integral equation method and binary Topology Optimization, a tool is proposed for the purposeful design of filters tailored to efficaciously mitigate Electromagnetic Interference (EMI).

articleTitle: Austin RCS Benchmarks: Validation Using Altair Feko
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Radar cross section (RCS) validation has been performed for Altair Feko by using University of Texas (UT) Austin RCS Benchmark Suite. Aircraft models are uncommon for public computational electromagnetic simulation validation. Lockheed Martin's AFRL EXPEDITE Program designed two aircraft models and made RCS measurements that have been made available to the public. UT Austin collaborated with Lockheed Martin to include these RCS measurements and aircraft models within their Benchmark Suite. In this paper, three aircraft models, PEC Closed Duct, Resin Closed Duct, and PEC Open Duct are simulated using Altair's computational electromagnetics software Feko to validate against UT Austin's ARCHIE-AIM code as well as measured data.

articleTitle: Implementation of Inhomogeneous Broadening in Time-Domain Dispersive Maxwell Solvers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present a general approach for implementing inhomogeneous broadening (time-dependent decay) in time do-main (TD) dispersive Maxwell solvers. The classical idealized Lorentz, Drude, and Debye models are extended to Gauss-Lorentz, Gauss-Drude, and Gauss-Debye models, respectively. The efficient TD implementation is developed employing mini-max optimized semi-analytical approximation (MiMOSA). It is rigorously tested for all models and experimental data with an in-house FDTD solver and commercial FDTD software.

articleTitle: RF-SoC Platforms for RF-AI Spectrum Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Sensing and perception of RF signals using AI is fundamental for future wireless systems. This paper describes measurable progress towards a truly wideband RF-AIIML spectrum perception testbed. We provide an approach for processing the 6–7 GHz range using 8-phase multirate processing on an RF-SoC. Up to 16 such 1 GHz channels can be accommodated on a ZCU-1275/1285 RF-SoC leading to an aggregate bandwidth of 16 GHz across the FRI/FR3 range. We aim to parallelize 16 GHz of aggregate bandwidth across the 100 MHz - 24 GHz spectrum into 512 data paths each having 32 MHz of bandwidth, such that a variety of AIIML based signal perception can operate in a massively parallel architecture on the FPGA.

articleTitle: Multistatic, Real-time, High Resolution Lunar Penetrating Imaging Approach for Water-Ice Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Since the confirmation of water-ice presence in the lunar subsurface at its poles, space programs such as NASA's Artemis program (2022) and India's Chandrayaan-3 (2023) aim to explore the interplanetary habitat of the Moon. High resolution stratigraphic subsurface mapping currently sought via lunar penetrating radar (LPR) are difficult to obtain using rovers with sensor emplacements across large areas. There are several challenges with past sub-surface mission soundings through LPR rovers. Besides the ubiquitous antenna coupling, it is difficult to obtain quality information from the LPR due to resolution and depth penetration limitations. Specifically, the resolution and penetration capabilities prevent a reliable study of lunar surface and subsurface properties. Notably, current imaging is done in situ and takes a long time to collect data over a short distance. Concerning lunar missions, Saturn's moon Titan has become a recent target as the presence of water has been confirmed along with hydrocarbons. Accordingly, the development of lunar unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) can be leveraged to improve sensitivity and resolution of planetary surface explorations. To this end, this paper proposes multi-look/multi-static lunar imaging via UAV swarms for water-ice detection. Unlike LPR rover exploration, UAVs are not susceptible to landform topologies and can easily navigate through scarps in areas of the Moon that are still unexplored. Additionally, the proposed multi-look approach can facilitate the collection of large data volumes in short time for a transformative lunar probing paradigm.

articleTitle: Comparison of Concrete Sample Scattering Parameters Obtained from FDTD and Microwave Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Concrete is the most widely used building material. Determining the dielectric properties of concrete is important since it is possible to comment on its mechanical properties by determining the dielectric properties of concrete. Dielectric constants can be determined thanks to the scattering parameters obtained at microwave frequencies using the free space technique. The reflection and transmission parameters of a cube-shaped concrete sample are measured by the free space method using the Vivaldi antenna array. The scattering parameters obtained from the finite difference time domain (FDTD) numerical method, which is commonly used to model electromagnetic wave propagation, are compared with the scattering parameters obtained from measurements and it is observed that both methods give effective results.

articleTitle: HFSS Enables Cold Plasma Simulation for RF and Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper considers the novel features of cold plasma as a user-defined material parameter in HFSS, which, in turn, allows engineers and scientists to explore the potential applications in the diversified areas of RF/microwave. Users can easily feed the plasma parameters of their interest and investigate the nature of wave-plasma interaction. As HFSS offers gold-standard electromagnetic simulation, this feature enables full-wave self-consistent EM wave propagation in a plasma medium. For illustration, in this paper, we have demonstrated the HFSS solution in communications blackout and designed a tunable power divider. Various details and many other case studies will be discussed at the conference.

articleTitle: Near Field Electromagnetic Interference Coupling-Mechanisms of Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, the electromagnetic coupling of a multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) to a closed transversal electromagnetic waveguide, used for standardized metrological characterization procedures in the field of electromagnetic compatibility, is investigated. The different coupling paths between the finger electrodes of the device under test (DUT) and the measurement device are characterized by numerical field simulations and measurements. The information gained makes it possible to distinguish between the two asymmetrical DUT electrodes that are not visible or distinguishable from the outside.

articleTitle: Numerical Accuracy of Circuit-Based Equations for Antenna Quality Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Electrically small antennas (ESAs) are known to have narrow impedance bandwidths. A long-standing means to quantify this trade-off between electrical size and bandwidth has been through the quality factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> of the antenna. Chu (L. J. Chu, “Physical limitations of omni-directional antennas,” J. Appl. Phys., vol. 19, no. 12, pp. 1163–1175, Dec. 1948) quantified this by expanding the wave impedances of spherical waves into lumped RLC circuits, whose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> can be computed directly by carrying out a circuit analysis for each spherical wave order. Chu also provided approximate expressions for general mode order, though these only converge onto the exact solution in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ka\rightarrow 0$</tex> limit, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> is the wavenumber and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> is the radius of the smallest sphere that circumscribes the antenna. Collin and Rothschild (R. E. Collin and S. Rothschild, “Evaluation of antenna <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Q}$</tex>,” IEEE Trans. Antennas Propag., vol. AP-12, no. 1, pp. 23–27, Jan. 1964) integrated directly over the same spherical waves (after subtracting the radiated fields) to obtain the stored energy of each spherical wave, and hence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>. Recently, Murray and Iyer (A. B. Murray and A. K. Iyer, “Analytical expressions for spherical wire antenna quality factor demonstrating exact agreement between circuit- based and field integration techniques,” IEEE Trans. Antennas Propag., vol. 72, no. 2, pp. 1636–1647, Feb. 2024) have shown that these two methods produce identical results, for all spherical wave orders <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> and electrical sizes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ka$</tex>.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies on Quasi-isotropic Circumferentially Short-circuited Magnetic Dipole Antennas with Different Flared Angles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A circumferentially short-circuited circular sector quasi-isotropic magnetic dipole antenna is proposed. Two prototypes with different flared angles are investigated and discussed. Both prototypes are fed by coaxial cables without and with a sleeve choke respectively and excited at 3.6 GHz. It has been experimentally proved that better radiation pattern in zyplane can be achieved with a relatively small flared angle and an incorporated sleeve choke, in which case the uniformity of the radiation pattern in zy-plane is enhanced by 6.9 dB.

articleTitle: Differentiable Inverse Design of Free- form Meta-optics Using Multiplicative Filter Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Recent developments in automatic differentiation enhance the inverse design methodologies for optimizing flexible and free-form meta-optical devices. This study introduces an inverse design framework that merges a fully differentiable rigorous diffraction interface theory solver with a multiplicative filter network, serving as a generator for free-form meta-atoms. The simulation outcomes confirm that our framework effectively meets its design objectives, optimizing two wide-band mid-infrared beam deflectors for TE and TM modes and enhancing transmission efficiencies to as much as 80% at target wavelengths.

articleTitle: Frequency- and Time-domain Green function methods for electromagnetic simulation, optimization, and design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present a family of numerical methods for the solution of Maxwell's equations, with application to simulation, optimization, and design. In particular, a novel rectangular-polar integral equation solver is mentioned which can produce solutions to the time harmonic Maxwell's equations, with high order accuracy, for general2D and 3D structures, with an extension to time domain problems on the basis of a time re-centering synthesis technique. An effective integral equation acceleration method, the IFGF method (Interpolated Factored Green Function), is used, which evaluates the action of Green function-based integral operators for an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> - point surface discretization at a computational cost of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N\log N)$</tex> operations without recourse to the FFT-thus, lending itself to effective distributed memory parallelization. Computational illustrations include applications to photonic optimization and design.

articleTitle: MESTI: Maxwell's Equations Solver with Thousands of Inputs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We describe our open-source software “Maxwell's equations solver with thousands of inputs,” (MESTI), which uses the “augmented partial factorization” (APF) method to enable full-wave single-shot computations for multi-source electromagnetic problems in one to three dimensions.

articleTitle: Using the Darwin Approximation for Equivalent Circuit Parameter Extraction with Frequency-dependent Linear Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, a simulation methodology is introduced, aimed at constructing an equivalent circuit (EC) for a device under investigation, specifically a common-/differential-mode ferrite choke. This methodology comprehensively incorporates resistive, inductive and capacitive effects by employing Darwin's approximation of Maxwell's equations and using Finite Element (FE) simulations, thus eliminating the need for time-consuming and costly measurement campaigns. This approach enables the efficient extension of classical and well-established eddy current simulations to include capacitive effects, while circumventing the complexities associated with electromagnetic wave phenomena such as the necessity of open domain boundary conditions. Especially in power electronic applications, the signal spectrum typically remains below the threshold frequency where wave effects become dominant, precisely the region covered by the Darwin model. Moreover, a frequency-dependent heuristic permeability model for the choke material is used, which enables the incorporation of typical quantities provided by manufacturers of ferrite materials.

articleTitle: A Phase-Informed p-Adaptation Method for Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel integral-equation-based method for electromagnetic scattering analysis. This method combines phase-extracted basis functions (PEBFs) with higher-order basis functions (HOBFs) to calculate scattering from electrically large and complex structures accurately and efficiently. In this method, a two-step procedure is applied to perform an adaptive p- refinement in mesh elements identified by a fast rough calculation using PEBFs on a coarse mesh. This is followed by a second step of calculation using HOBFs only in elements that need refinement. This approach significantly reduces computational costs while maintaining the simulation accuracy for modeling complex geometries. Electromagnetic scattering from a spherical cavity is used as an example to demonstrate the performance of this method.

articleTitle: Frequency-time hybrid method in exterior and interior domains
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present a frequency/time hybrid integral-equation method [1, 2] for the time-dependent wave equation in two and three-dimensional spatial domains, possibly including closed cavities.

articleTitle: Design of A Cavity-Backed 360° Beam Steerable Antenna for 5G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A wideband steerable antenna design with high gain is a formidable problem. This work proposes a cube-shaped cavitybacked dual-band antenna demonstrating 360° beam steering capability. The proposed antenna operates from 3.68 GHz to 4.72 GHz frequency range with a notch at 4.1 GHz. The antenna offers an 8 dBi peak gain. In addition, an electronically controlled frequency selective surface has been designed to replace the cavity's metallic faces, allowing 360-degree electronic beam steerability. The electronic steerability of the proposed antenna suggests its applicability in mobile communication and UAV applications.

articleTitle: Description of a 2D Experimental Machine-learning Microwave Dataset and Initial Supervised Descent Method Imaging Results
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We describe an experimentally collected 2D microwave imaging dataset comprising of 5 dielectric and metallic targets. We also use the Supervised Descent imaging method (trained exclusively on experimental data) to provide preliminary imaging results.

articleTitle: A Spatial-LDI $\Delta-\Sigma$ LNA Design in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Low noise and maximum linearity are critical for aperture array receivers. Receiver sensitivity and resilience to jamming are fundamentally limited by LNA noise figure (NF) and linearity, respectively. This paper describes the preliminary design of a wideband 65 nm CMOS LNA and signal processing circuits for spatial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta-\Sigma$</tex> noise shaping to improve both NF and linearity when used in array apertures. The design exploits the 2D spatiotemporal frequency domain properties of plane-waves for noise and distortion shaping. MATLAB simulations indicate an NF improvement of 3.9 dB over a 5 GHz bandwidth for 20 dB LNA gain and 2× spatial over-sampling. Transistor-level simulation results of the 65 nm CMOS blocks are also provided.

articleTitle: Design of 3-bit Angle-Insensitive RIS for 5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper introduces a 3-bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) design characterized by its unique angle-insensitive properties for 5G communication systems. The proposed configuration provides eight distinct phase states enabled by the states of two varactors with an applied bias voltage. The design of the unit cell with double centric square split ring resonators and the formation of the RIS with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 5$</tex> array have been presented. A detailed analysis of the RIS performance has been conducted using the CST 3D electromagnetic simulator to study the reflection amplitude and phase responses. It is demonstrated that the results show a phase range of up to 315 degrees, along with eight distinct states exhibiting a stable interval of 45 degrees. This effectively covers incidence angles ranging from 0 to 60 degrees.

articleTitle: A Simple Algebraic Method to Solve the Matrix Equation Generated by the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, we present a new solution procedure to solve the matrix equation generated by the well-known method of moments (MOM). The first step involves approximating the given structure via standard geometrical discretization and defining the conventional basis functions to approximate the induced current. The second step involves gathering the total number of basis functions into a small number of groups thereby casting the moment matrix into a collection of smaller matrices representing self and mutual interactions between the groups. Third, the procedure sets the matrix blocks residing on either side of the diagonal block to zero using straight-forward mathematical steps. Finally, the new matrix equation is solved efficiently using simple algebraic steps.

articleTitle: R-LRCBNet: A YOLOV8-based Oriented Ship Detection Method of SAR Image
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Ship targets in SAR images are characterized by the remarkable features of multi-scale, arbitrary orientation and dense arrangement, which is a great challenge for fast and accurate target detection. In order to solve problems, we propose a YOLOV8-based oriented ship detection method of SAR image with lightweight receptor field feature convolution (LRFAConv) and bottleneck transformers (R-LRCBNet) in this paper. Firstly, we use the probabilistic intersection-over-union (ProbIoU) loss function in the angle prediction branch to train angle information. Secondly, global spatial self-attention mechanism is proposed to optimise the network enhancement feature information. This method alleviates the effects of suppressing complex background interference and vessel distribution. Finally, we take the yolov8-n model as the baseline. The LRFAConv is used to instead of a convolutional layer to reduce the model parameters. The average accuracy of the proposed method on the complex scene dataset SRSDD is 71.8%, the F1 score is 70.51, and the model size is 6.8M, which is better than other 8 comparison models.

articleTitle: Hessian-based Antenna Optimization with Automatic Differentiation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Recently [1], there has been a significant interest in the design of antenna systems driven by the emergence of new requirements in areas such as 5G and 6G communications, Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, and radar technologies. Antennas are expected to meet specifications such as higher radiation efficiency, agile beam steering, broader bandwidths, and multiband operation. Due to these increasingly challenging requirements, global optimization techniques such as the genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and simulated annealing (SA) are often employed to find an antenna design that satisfies the specified objectives. In all these methods, the information gathered by individual agents or swarms is shared with other elements, thereby enhancing their search capabilities. Global methods do not require an initial guess, making them ideal for problems lacking a good initial design. However, they suffer from poor computational efficiency, as they require a significant number of function evaluations to find an optimum solution.

articleTitle: Advancements in Wearable MagnetoCardioGraphy (MCG) Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: MagnetoCardioGraphy (MCG) is a technique used to detect the heart's naturally emanated magnetic fields. Given the weak level of these signals, state-of-the-art MCG devices are costly, bulky, and/or require shielding. More recently, our research has demonstrated wearable MCG sensors that overcome these limitations. In this paper, we review the operating principle of these wearable MCG sensors and discuss the advancements in technology over the past years. The ultimate goal is to inspire further design optimization and clinical applications.

articleTitle: On the Numerical Modeling of Tapered Anechoic Ranges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Since their introduction in the late 1960s Tapered Anechoic Chambers have become popular tools for the measurement of antenna patterns at frequencies under 1 GHz. Since their inception several papers mention the fact that these chambers did not have a spherical wave propagation and thus, the Friis transmission equation to measure gain cannot be applied. This knowledge was presented in 1967 by King et al. and was based on measurements performed at X-band inside a scaled tapered anechoic range. In this paper numerical methods are applied to confirm the findings of the 1960s paper using different models of tapered ranges at different frequencies. While the results confirm the findings of the 1960s paper, they also validate some of the theories about the operation of these antenna ranges.

articleTitle: A Marching -on-Frequency - Inspired Cascaded Network for Multi-frequency Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A cascaded machine learning model designed to produce target images from multi-frequency microwave imaging data is presented. The architecture is inspired by a marching-on-frequency approach where lower frequency information is used to recover lower resolution images that are used as initial guesses or prior information at higher frequencies. The architecture consists of a sequence of U-net-like deep learning models, each taking single-frequency microwave measurement data and the reconstruction from the previous model in the sequence as input. For both synthetic and experimental imaging scenarios the cascaded network is shown to out-perform a data-to-image network where the same multi-frequency data is incorporated as a multi-channel input.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Inverse Design of Superchiral Dielectric Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Chirality is a fundamental property of asymmetry and is crucial in distinguishing molecular enantiomers, with profound implications across chemistry, biology, and materials science. Circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy, which measures the differential absorption of left-handed (LCP) and right-handed (RCP) circularly polarized light, serves as a conventional method for identifying and separating chiral enantiomers. Nevertheless, due to the inherently weak chiral-optical interactions, the CD signals of numerous chiral molecules are minimal, typically spanning 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> within the ultraviolet spectrum. Superchiral metasurfaces, producing fields with enhanced optical chirality that surpasses the chirality of circularly polarized light, emerge as a solution to this challenge. Such metasurfaces, with enhanced interaction between light and chiral molecules, offer a significant increase in CD signal, underscoring the necessity for their advanced development for more accurate and sensitive analysis. This study presents a novel, two-stage inverse design methodology for superchiral metasurfaces with iterative optimization of the topology of a dielectric metasurface unit cell to enhance optical chiral density in the near field. In the first stage, a neural network-based optimizer works in tandem with a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) solver. In the second stage, adjoint gradients of the optical chirality density are derived from the first principles and calculated with a Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) scheme. Our results offer a new platform for high-sensitivity CD spectroscopy applications, allowing for fast, constrained optimization of the unit cells.

articleTitle: Advanced Shielding To Suppress Magnetic Field Emission For Improved Hardware Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Multilayered stacks of conducting and magnetic films are investigated as electromagnetic interference (EMI) shields to suppress noise in power electronic packages. Graphene nanoplatelets (GNP) and nickel are used to represent the two systems. Four layers of GNP- Ni of 4 µm, each layer of 1 µmthickness, provide shielding effectiveness (SE) of 8–53 dB based on the NSA 65–6 standard across 1–100 MHz. The same stack design shows a SE of 45–80 dB based on the IEEE 299 standards at the same frequency range. The proposed four-layer EMI shield is a suitable implementation in the power inductors to mitigate their unintended magnetic field. Also, a monolithic GNP shield can be implemented between the switching element and the heat sink. Thus, parasitic capacitance effects can be reduced, particularly the common mode radiation. Furthermore, this approach mitigates the hot spots due to the GNP's higher thermal conductivity.

articleTitle: A Wideband Reconfigurable Reflectarray Using the Frequency Pulling Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, we present an elegant, simple to fabricate and very cost effective technique for designing wide-band reconfigurable reflectarray antennas. First, we utilize our recently proposed frequency pulling technique (FPT) to increase the bandwidth of reflectarray antennas (RAs). Notably, based on FPT, a simple feeding network is properly designed and connected at the backplane of each RA's unit cell. In turn, we connect readily available diodes to this feeding network properly changing its electrical characteristics and applying the desired reconfigurability. To demonstrate our technique we utilize a traditional microstrip patch element. Specifically, we (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>) apply our FPT method feeding each unit cell at two properly selected feed points and achieving a 28% fractional (gain) bandwidth, and (b) use a single diode to reconfigure the RA's beams between 30O and -30° in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi=0^{{\circ}}$</tex> plane. Our designed RA shows great beam stability for both beam states within its entire 8.85 GHz to 11.75 GHz bandwidth of operation.

articleTitle: Analytical Green's Functions for Two-Dimensional Electrostatics and Boundary-Element Based Solver
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We derive analytical Green's functions for two-dimensional (2D) electrostatic problem, based on which a boundary-element based 2D electrostatic solver is developed. The system is composed of perfect electric conductors and linear dielectric materials; the boundary conditions are specified by an applied field and the total charge of each conductor. The solver is benchmarked by computing the macroscopic parameter of the system and comparing them to the exact values. Two applications are considered. First we determine the characteristic impedance of a microstrip transmission line; the results agree well with established values in literature. Second we compute the sensitivity of the field-induced torque with respect to the shape deformation. The consistent results using the finite difference and the adjoint method indicate that our solver is sufficiently precise to tell the fine difference from two very similar shapes.

articleTitle: Accurate Modeling for Electromagnetic Interaction with Plasma-Surrounded Metallic Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) interaction with plasma-surrounded metallic objects will occur when the re-entry capsule of space craft re-entries the atmospheric layer and its accurate modeling and analysis are very desirable. The integral equation method is used to govern the problem and the volume-surface integral equations are needed to describe the involved EM characteristic since the objects include both the impenetrable conductor and penetrable conductive plasma. The VSIEs are usually solved by the method of moments (MoM), but it may not be feasible when considering the changeable shape of plasmoid cluster. To this end, a truly meshless method (TMM) is proposed to solve the VSIEs with such an object. The TMM employs a virtual cylinder to enclose the object and transforms the volume integral over the cylinder into a surface integral over its boundaries based on Green-Gauss theorem. This transformation is equivalent to switch the change of geometric shape into the change of material distribution in the volume. A numerical example is presented to illustrate the method and its good performance has been verified.

articleTitle: Parallel Fast Iterative H-Matrix-Accelerated Locally Corrected Nyström Method with an Unreliable H-matrix Based Preconditioner
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this study, we introduce a fast, error controllable and parallel iterative technique for dealing with the Combined Field Integral Equation (CFIE) using the Locally Corrected Nyström (LCN) method. We use a less precise H-matrix, derived from the coefficient matrix, as a preconditioner in a linear iterative method. This inaccurate preconditioner, which includes less precision in both constructing the H-matrix and inverting the resulting matrix, significantly speeds up the process of solving the system. However, it's important to note that this accelerated approach has notable effects on the residual and accuracy of the problem, which introduces a challenge in effectively addressing the complexities associated with solving the CFIE.

articleTitle: Real-Time Computation of E-Field for Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) is a non-invasive brain stimulation technique employing coils to induce electric fields (E-fields) in the brain, influencing its activity. Accurately determining the dosage of E-field induced in targeted brain areas during TMS is crucial for evaluating its effects and optimizing parameters such as coil current amplitude and placement. We present a method capable of computing induced E-fields for arbitrary coil positions in real-time (within 4 milliseconds) within the brain. Initially, white noise currents, defined on a surface delineating the head and its surrounding medium, are employed to generate a comprehensive basis set of mode field patterns representing TMS-induced brain E-fields. Subsequently, electromagnetic reciprocity and Huygens' principles are leveraged to establish the relationship between expansion coefficients for these modes and TMS-induced electric fields in free space. Our real-time TMS solver predicts E-fields with comparable accuracy to existing solvers using fewer than 400 modes, rendering it suitable for neuronavigation systems and real-time adjustment of coil dosing parameters.

articleTitle: Analyzing Electromagnetic Pulse Diffraction for the Reconstruction of Elliptical Cylinder Shapes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This study focused on analyzing the effectiveness of Gaussian radio pulse for dielectric object detection and reconstruction in diffraction phenomena. The study utilized MATLAB to create a program for generating animation illustrating dynamic changes in the field distribution on a 2D plane, specifically focusing on interactions with dielectric objects and identifying the first and second echo states over time in recorded snapshots. In addition, based on the first and second echo values obtained, an algorithm was presented to reconstruct the dielectric object shape. The study demonstrated the precise reconstruction of objects, such as circular and elliptical cylinders, by applying a Gaussian radio pulse, showcasing the potential accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Differential Arrays for Butler Multi-Beam STAR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) over the same frequency range enables in-band full duplex (IBFD) communication with doubled spectral efficiency. This paper presents an IBFD system that connects an antenna array with a multi-beam former to decrease the impact of the self-interference (SI) existing between the transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) in a multiple input and multiple output (MIMO) system. Physical symmetry is used to cancel near-field coupling. Reflections of the Tx from the surrounding environment usually leak into the receive antennas to cause SI with long delay-bandwidth products that are notoriously hard to remove; the proposed differential array greatly reduces such interference.

articleTitle: Miniaturizing Microstrip Antennas Using the Frequency Pulling Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Antenna miniaturization is traditionally achieved at the expense of bandwidth. In this work, we show the feasibility of miniaturizing microstrip antennas without compromising their bandwidth. Namely, we achieve that by utilizing our recently presented frequency pulling technique. To showcase the effective-ness of our method, we apply it to a microstrip patch antenna. Specifically, by utilizing our technique, we successfully decrease its aperture size by a factor of four while maintaining both its original height and bandwidth.

articleTitle: GPU Acceleration Using CUDA for Computational Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Although initially designed for graphics rendering applications, Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), due to their massively parallel many-core nature, have seen widespread use in accelerating many computationally expensive algorithms in recent years. In particular, GPUs have revolutionized the field of machine learning, enabling training deep neural network models which are multiple orders of magnitude larger than previously possible. Even consumer-grade GPUs, which have become very affordable and can be found in personal workstations (e.g., the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090), can achieve upwards of 80 TeraFLOPS computing performance.

articleTitle: A Novel Neural Point Field Framework for End-to-End Wireless Channel Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel neural wireless channel modeling methodology by leveraging a point-cloud-based neural network. During the training phase, the proposed method learns the interaction between wireless transceivers and their environment with wave propagation properties. After training, our work serves as a neural forward model for rapidly predicting the wireless channel for new transceiver locations. As such, it establishes an end-to-end pipeline for network planning and deployment optimization. A noteworthy aspect of our approach lies in the intriguing point-cloud-based neural framework, allowing seamless generalization to large-scale scenes.

articleTitle: Effect of Radii of Curvature in Flexible Substrates on the Performance of Super-Wideband Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Flexible substrates are gaining popularity in wireless communications due to their adaptability and lightweight properties. However, microstrip patch antennas, traditionally fabricated on rigid dielectric substrates, have exhibited super-wideband characteristics and high boresight gain. The demand for flexible substrate-based super-wideband patch antennas is growing, especially for unmanned aerial vehicle applications. This paper explores the impact of various flexible substrates (Rogers 5880T, Rogers 3003C, and Polyethylene Terephthalate) and different radii of curvature (flat to 45 mm bend) on the super-wideband response (from L to K-band) of an edge-fed circular patch antenna. The study also presents antenna gain and radiation efficiency results to assess the influence of flexible substrates. The findings indicate that Rogers 3003C maintains a super-wideband response with adequate gain up to a 45 mm radius of curvature.

articleTitle: Metasurface Characterization for Low Frequency Shielding Purposes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The purpose of the present study is to ensure that a metasurface, consisting of a 5×5 array of resonating coils at different frequencies, owns shielding properties in the frequency range adopted by Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems for automotive applications, i.e. kHz frequency range. The dimensions of the slab and the individual unit cell tailored for the system have been chosen to completely cover a pre-existing small-scale WPT system at low frequencies, since a WPT system had been previously developed by the authors in an earlier study. The unit cell of the array is made up of a solenoid featuring M = 30 turns, crafted from enamel-coated copper wire with a gauge of AWG28 (equivalent to a wire diameter of 0.315mm). The solenoid has a diameter (D) of 4 cm and a height (h) of 11.05mm. The metasurface has a total surface equal to 20 cm x 20 cm. (M. Simonazzi, L. Sandrolini, S. Barmada, and N. Fontana, “Optimal Metamaterial Configuration for Magnetic Field Shielding in Wireless Power Transfer Systems,” 2023 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE), San Diego, CA, USA, 2023, pp. 1–5, doi: 10.1109/WPTCE56855.2023.10216186). A numerical FEKO model has been implemented and simulated with this purpose. The results in terms of Shielding Effectiveness (SE) within the interested frequency range have demonstrated that the metasurface behaves as a shield around 105kHz: the last properties can be obtained by exploiting the symmetry of the system and by tuning each unitcell at 6 different frequencies in the interested frequency range, with 6 different capacitors obtained by an optimization performed at steady-state regime. The SE has been evaluated with two simulations: one in which two simple non resonating coils are fed in unloaded conditions of use and one in which the metasurface has been inserted between the coils (Fig. 1 (left)). In both cases the scattering parameter S21 has been evaluated. The shielding effectiveness in logarithmic scale has been determined, as in Eq. (1) and shown in Fig. 1 (right). At the conference, an early-stage prototype of the metasurface will be presented and further details about its electrical properties will be provided by the use of measurements.

articleTitle: Battery-less, Multichannel and Wireless Recorder for Neuronal Activity Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Continuous intracranial monitoring of neural activity is used to map the seizure onset zone in epilepsy patients. In this paper, we propose a novel battery-free and multichannel wireless neurosensing system (m WiNS). For the first time, a miniaturized well packaged passive multichannel recorder matched to high impedance commercial electrodes is presented. The proposed packaged implant allows for full implantation in animals such as swine. Our smaller antenna for different skin depth shows improvement over previous designs. Benchtop measurements indicate correct recovery of the neural signals, demonstrating the implant capabilities for neural epilepsy indicators of our proposed wireless system.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Deployable Inverted-Hat Monopole Antenna via Artificial Transmission Line Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The integration of High Frequency (HF) antennas into large structures faces challenges related to size and mechanical limitations, primarily because of their substantial dimensions. Also, large HF antennas pose issues such as higher lightning strike risk, diminished transmission efficiency, and costly maintenance. In this context, this paper proposes a novel approach of three-fold miniaturization for an inverted-hat monopole (IHM) antenna (A. D. Johnson, J. A. Caripidis, S. B. Venkatakrishnan, M. Ali and J. L. Volakis, “Deployable Inverted-Hat Monopole With 3:1 Constant Gain Bandwidth,” in IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters, vol. 19, no. 6, pp. 935–938, June 2020) through artificial transmission line (ATL) loading (J.L. Volakis, C.C Chen and K. Fujimoto, Small Antennas: Miniaturization Techniques and Applications, 448pp, McGraw-Hill, 2010). An ATL incorporating inductive and capacitive loads, and appropriate phase variations among segments, is proposed for miniaturization of ultra-wideband antenna bandwidth. A tuned ATL can be loaded into existing compact antennas and for further size reduction. To realize this approach, we considered the already developed low-profile <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda_{LOW}/7.5)$</tex> top-loaded monopole antenna by A.D. Johnson et al. (2020). The IHM antenna is deployable, and its input impedance is controllable. Further, the antenna's top copper layer is replaced by a series of inductors (L) with shunt capacitors (C) arms (see Fig. 1). The latter loading allows for the simultaneous control of impedance and phase velocity, providing two degrees of freedom for wideband matching. A full-wave simulation with Ansys HFSS showed that a standalone 1.0m tall IHM with a reactive loading hat <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{L}=10\mu \mathrm{F}$</tex> and C = 90 nF) operates from 15MHz to 50MHz with a VSWR < 3. Meanwhile, an umbrella-folding is adopted for packaging the IHM with reactive loading. The average gain across the bandwidth is around 3.5 dBi while the antenna is fully deployed. The deployed volume of this reactive ATL loaded inverted-hat monopole antenna is 60 cm x 60 cm x 100 cm.

articleTitle: Group-Level Optimum Coil Placement for Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) stands as a widely employed non-invasive method for both medical treatment and scientific investigation, granted approval by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the USA for clinical use. Precisely targeting and dosing the electromagnetic field (E-field) induced by TMS remains crucial due to its non-invasive nature. Clinical TMS often relies on scalp landmarks based on EEG coordinate systems, yet anatomical differences among individuals can lead to varied brain targets for the same scalp landmark, limiting TMS efficacy. To address this, one proposed solution involves creating a comprehensive database of head models to optimize E-field dosimetry at target locations, but this requires extensive computational simulations across subjects and coil models, which can be impractical.

articleTitle: Safety of Wireless Brain Implants: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Advancements in self-powering and power transfer have brought promising solutions for stimulation or sensing applications within the brain without the need for continuous guided mediums. However, employing entirely wireless brain implants may result in novel risks such as implant migration and adverse neural tissue interactions. The available scientific literature is evaluated and investigated to determine the biological safety implications associated with wireless brain implants. Following PRISMA guidelines, electronic database searches were conducted to identify suitable literature. Findings illustrate advancements in computing technology and human head simulations that show promise in achieving safety standards set by governing authorities and acute medical complications are exceedingly rare. However, lack of clarity around wireless device induced psychological stress, a shortfall in specialized radio-frequency engineers and accurate human head modeling, and documented issues with a lack of uniform testing consensus, warrants considerable caution until the quality of experimental methodology in subsequent studies is improved to the degree necessary to deduce needed clarity on these safety issues.

articleTitle: A Flexible Ku-Band Checkerboard Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The design of a flexible and conformal phased array antenna for Ku-band was presented in this paper. Flexible DuPont PCBs and rigid Rogers PCBs were arranged in a checkerboard configuration. This enables the array antenna to be flexible in either x- or y-axis. A prototype flexible checkerboard array antenna was fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Use of the Extended BLT Equation for ElectromagneticWave Coupling Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The growth of high-speed electronic and wireless systems has increased the threat of both unintentional and intentional electromagnetic interference (EMI/IEMI). Analyses of the coupling of electromagnetic waves onto the conductors of electrical systems, are needed in order to accurately determine the susceptibility of both simple and complex electronic devices. Current technology allows for these devices' CAD models to be evaluated in an electromagnetic simulator, where both their radiative and non-radiative responses to their environment are observed. However, an increase in the complexity of the models increases the computational cost of the simulation. Reduction in the simulation's time and memory usage is achieved through the use of transmission line methods. This study serves to determine the coupling of an electromagnetic plane wave onto a uniform transmission line above a ground plane. The transmission line is terminated with load resistances comparable to practical loads. Excitation of the line is produced by an EM wave that is normal to the ground plane, with an electric field that is linearly polarized, and oriented in the direction of the lateral face of the transmission line. Inclusion of a ground plane introduces an additional EM wave source that is reflected from the ground plane. Although delayed, it is combined with the incident plane wave from the source through the use of a Green's function derived by Tesche and Butler (F. M. Tesche and C. M. Butler, Interaction Notes, Note 588). The voltages and currents induced on these transmission lines from the field sources are calculated using the Extended-BLT (Baum-Liu- Tesche) Equation derived in the same literature. This multi-conductor transmission-line method, allows for the topography of the system to be converted into matrices and super matrices, in order to solve for the propagating voltage and current along the lines. This methodology is derived in the notes of Carl Baum (C. E. Baum, T. K. Liu, and F. M. Tesche, Interaction Notes, EMP-3, Notes 1-635), this being the traditional BLT equation. To verify these results, a full wave EM solver is used to simulate the setup, along with experimental measurements. Modifications to the Green's functions provided by Tesche, Keen and Butler (F. M. Tesche, J. M. Keen, and C. M. Butler, URSI Radio Sci., 312, pp. 32-47), are necessary since a finite ground plane is used in the experimental setup. This work looks to further this approach with wide frequency-range coverage, along with near-field effects, with excitation from oblique incidence angles, and the effects of polarization utilizing the methods found in various texts (specifically F. M. Tesche, M. V. Ianoz, and T. Karlsson, John Wiley and Sons, pp. 183-217). In doing so attempts to extend the BLT equation further to include a transmission line enclosed in a structure with a large conductance, along with an aperture are made. Applying techniques from texts by Tesche, allows for a dyadic Green's function to be used based off the geometric properties of the aperture. This Green's function is then incorporated into the BLT equation to produce the excitation source of the transmission line enclosed in the conductor.

articleTitle: Higher Order Mortar Methods for the EFIE using Parametric Curved Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A variety of methods have been proposed for the solution of the discontinuous electric field integral equation (EFIE) for nonconformal meshes. Many of these methods (such as the discontinuous Galerkin and monopole method) involve the computation of expensive line integrals that alter the traditional impedance matrix entries. However, the mortar method has the benefits of involving simple line integrals over adjacent cells and concatenating those integrals onto the existing impedance matrix. As a result, the complexity of computation is limited to that of the corresponding basis sets along the boundary (i.e. without Green's functions and the corresponding singularities), and the original impedance matrix is still available for re-use or for direct processing, as in characteristic mode analysis. Prior studies have demonstrated that the mortar method and monopole methods produce similar answers for surface currents across boundaries. It has similarly been shown that the extension of the mortar method to higher-order basis sets converges to similar current values as the conformal solutions over the same geometries.

articleTitle: New Features in Altair Feko 2023
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper describes some of the new features in the commercial electromagnetic software Altair Feko. These include the domain decomposition method (DDM) for non-conformal meshes, characteristic basis function method (CBFM) to reduce the number of unknowns, extending the characteristic mode analysis (CMA) to include lossy dielectrics, and improving the combined method of moments (MoM) and multiconductor transmission line (MTL) cable harness solution.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Different Phase-Gradient Metasurface Unit Cells for Wide Angle Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Designing a wideband metasurface unit cell that exhibits phase gradient characteristics for beam steering applications is a big challenge. This research investigates the beam steering performance of three individual single-layered unit cells: (i) modified square (MS), (ii) modified hexagonal (MH), (iii) concentrated square hexagonal (CSH), and their corresponding multi-layered counterparts. These unit cells pose wideband phase gradient characteristics (19-22%) along with high transmission magnitude (> 0.9). These phase gradient metasurface (PGMS) unit cells are then integrated with an antenna and 55°, 30° and 55° maximum beam steerability obtained for modified square, modified hexagonal and concentrated square hexagonal cell, respectively. These unit cells can be used in Satellite and mobile communication for beam steering applications.

articleTitle: Array Failure Diagnosis via Characteristic Mode Theory and Near-Field Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, a novel reconstruction method for diagnosing faulty array elements is presented. Specifically, we demonstrate that by using characteristic mode analysis we can significantly reduce the ill-posed nature of an arbitrarily defined source-reconstruction problem. Our proposed method is validated through the diagnosis of a Yagi-Uda and an elliptical loop array, where suitable reconstructions are obtained.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Worst-Case Waveform Coupling to a Loaded System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Waveforms that maximize coupling to linear loads have been theoretically synthesized but have not been experimentally validated. These waveforms can be calculated using the device's frequency domain transfer function. This work aims to experimentally validate the RF coupling performance of these theoretical worst-case waveforms to a device composed of concentric copper loops loaded with a nonlinear diode. Experimental results show that the worst-case broadband excitation generates a coupled voltage double that of narrowband excitation. However, the same waveform only couples~ 25% of the energy of a narrowband waveform centered at the peak of the device's transfer function. This work provides the first experimental validation of the coupling performance of optimized waveforms.

articleTitle: Recent Algorithm Developments in the ButterflyPACK Package
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: ButterflyPACK (https://github.com/liuyangzhuan/ButterflyPACK) is an open-source high-performance computing software for compressing dense operators and solving linear systems arising from the discretization of 2D and 3D Maxwell and Helmholtz problems of integral equation (IE) or differential equation (DE) forms. ButterflyPACK (and its integration into sparse direct solver STRUMPACK) have been designed to easily interface with existing IE, FEM, FDFD codes (in C/C++/Fortran) only requiring either a user-supplied function to sample any matrix entry or apply the matrix to arbitrary vectors, or a sparse matrix (FEM/FDFD).

articleTitle: Simulations of the 5G Beamforming Performance for mm Wave Bands in an Urban Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The future information society will rely on 5G mobile communications to provide a wide variety of applications including completely new industrial and professional services. In order to meet these challenges, significantly higher mobile data throughputs are required which is possible by using higher frequency bands in the mmWave domain. The beamforming technique is applied to compensate for the higher pathloss due to the larger frequency and improve the signal quality. A practical application test case of beamforming in mm Wave 5G bands in an urban scenario is presented in this study.

articleTitle: A T-Matrix EFIE-PMCHWT Method for Computing Electromagnetic Scattering from Composite Conductor-Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The T-matrix (transition matrix) method is a widely used technique for modelling the electromagnetic scattering response from arbitrary shaped and sized scatterers and obstacles (M. I. Mishchenko, L. D. Travis and A. A. Lacis, Scattering, Absorption, and Emission of Light by Small Particles, 1st Ed, Cambridge University Press, 2002). While the technique has been employed for decades within the microwave and optical communities, formulations linking the T -matrix method and Integral Equations (IE) are relatively rare. An integrated formulation that combines the T -matrix method and Integral Equations is essential for testcases where the aspect ratio of the scattering geometry is skewed, or when conventional methods to extract the T -matrix fail.

articleTitle: Optimizing Antenna Element Distribution for Enhanced Gain in Sparse Array Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper introduces an array thinning technique for a 25-element antenna array at 5.4 GHz arranged in a 5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 5$</tex> grid. The aim is to reduce array size, weight, cost, and power by eliminating excess elements while preserving gain. We demonstrate that thinning the array to 9 elements (viz. a 64% reduction) has minimal impact on the realized gain. We explore various 9-element configurations using a genetic algorithm to validate our presented configuration. The best configuration incurs only a 1.82 dB loss at the broadside compared to a fully populated array. Prototypes were fabricated and measured, confirming excellent agreement with simulation results.

articleTitle: An Intuitive Evaluation Method of 1-Bit Reconfigurable Metasurface Element Based on Radiation Viewpoint
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper introduces a radiation viewpoint to evaluate reconfigurable metasurface (RMS) elements. By converting a conventional viewpoint structure to a radiation antenna, this method allows for a quantitative evaluation of RMS elements. Employing this innovative viewpoint, the paper proposes a several evaluation curves on the Smith chart, which can evaluate the RMS performances quantitatively and intuitively. This viewpoint and evaluation method can significantly enhance the design efficiency of RMS elements.

articleTitle: Sensor Data Relay System for Underground Mine Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A relay system to transfer pressure sensor data from a rotating drum of a continuous mining machine to a non-rotating nearby station is developed. Data collected from individual sensor-equipped pick cutters are grouped and fed to a CAN-BUS network. Data is transmitted out of this network via a 2.4GHz RF transmitter. A pair of high gain circularly polarized antennas are designed with protective covers to act as transmit and receive endpoints for the RF transmission.

articleTitle: An Intuitive Evaluation Method of 1-Bit Reconfigurable Metasurface Element Based on Radiation Viewpoint
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper introduces a radiation viewpoint to eval-uate reconfigurable metasurface (RMS) elements. By converting a conventional viewpoint structure to a radiation antenna, this method allows for a quantitative evaluation of RMS elements. Employing this innovative viewpoint, the paper proposes a several evaluation curves on the Smith chart, which can evaluate the RMS performances quantitatively and intuitively. This viewpoint and evaluation method can significantly enhance the design efficiency of RMS elements.

articleTitle: Scattering Analysis of Aircrafts of Different Sizes Using Altair Feko
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Radar detection or non-detection depends on the scattering of EM waves from different size aircraft such as drones, fighter jets and commercial jets. Different solver technologies are required for scattering analysis depending on the electrical size of the aircraft. In this paper, different aircraft structures are simulated in terms of the computational resource requirements for their scattering performance using the full wave and asymptotic EM solvers (MoM, ACA, MLFMM, PO and RL-GO) of the commercial EM tool, Altair Feko.

articleTitle: Group-based Compression of an FMM for Smooth Kernels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The fast multipole method (FMM) representation of matrices obtained by sampling smooth translationally invariant kernels can be compressed using a level-dependent iterative procedure. Here “level” is used to refer to a level of an underlying octree. In this presentation it is shown that additional compression is obtained if the level-based compression is subsequently applied to each octree group at each level. The additional compression is most significant for geometric configurations characterized by a non-uniform distribution of the underlying degrees of freedom (DOF). The compressed FMM representation retains translational invariance and there is no increase in the total number of translators.

articleTitle: Model Order Reduction Approach for PCB Structures based on Semi-discretized Darwin Model using FEM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The generation of reduced order models describing the input-output behavior of linear quasi-stationary electromagnetic field problems coupled with lumped elements is of particular interest, for example, in the field of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) investigations such as conducted emission predictions for printed circuit boards (PCB). Therefore, this article proposes the construction of a linear differential-algebraic equation (DAE) using the semi-discretization of a linear Darwin model with finite elements, whereby the Darwin model is an approximation of the full set of Maxwell's equations incorporating resistive, inductive and capacitive effects. This linear DAE has the advantages that it enables the application of various linear model order reduction (MOR) techniques and that the full and reduced order model (ROM) can be easily coupled with lumped elements. The pro-posed approach is applied to a realistic linear 4-layer PCB layout incorporating 4 linear components implemented with prescribed material parameter as well as an external linear discrete resistor resulting in a linear DAE with a single input voltage and a single output current. Applying the rational Krylov MOR method leads to a ROM with satisfying broadband approximation and a high compression ratio regarding the degrees of freedom (DOF).

articleTitle: Automated Pixelated Unit Cell Design for Reflectarray Antennas and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper we demonstrate an automated simulation process using Ansys's High Frequency Structures Simulator (HFSS) tool and MATLAB to generate unit cell configurations for specific phase distributions required for reflectarray antenna and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) designs. While this technique can be extended to any unit cell topology this paper focuses on randomly generated pixelated unit cells. The random pixelization is generated using MATLAB which is then fed to HFSS to evaluate the cell's reflected wave amplitude and phase. The phase values are screened to ensure that their corresponding reflected wave amplitudes are in the order of 90% before storing the cell configuration in a design database.

articleTitle: Analysis of Three-dimensional Composite Penetrable Scatterers Featuring mono-isotropic Impedance Sheets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this study, we present a novel method for analyzing composite penetrable scatterers featuring mono-isotropic imped-ance sheets, employing the method of moments (MoM). The problem is delineated into interior and exterior regions and tackled by employing the surface equivalence theorem along with boundary conditions to derive matrix equation solutions of the governing in-tegral equations.

articleTitle: A Numerical Study on EMI Shielding Strategies for LV Battery Pack Components
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, several shielding strategies are proposed and evaluated to prevent the common mode noise from the high voltage (HV) electrical architecture due to inverter switching from interfering with the performance of low voltage (LV) battery electronics and controllers. The battery pack of electric vehicles are generally compact, and the HV-LV components are typically in proximity inside the battery enclosure leading to a higher noise coupling. An approach to create a representative model for the victim PCB is presented. Three different practical shielding strategies are presented and analyzed for reducing electromagnetic interference (EMI) on the victim PCB, i.e. (i) Floating shield, (ii) Grounded shield and (iii) Box Shield.

articleTitle: Design of 145 GHz BPSK SDR on RF-SoC
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Wireless links at sub-THz bands require low-SWaP SDR modems. We report early design experimentation of an SDR operating in the 130–150 GHz band, with ASK/BPSK/QPSK modulation on I/Q channels, at a maximum data rate of 128 Mbps. The design utilizes 110–170 GHz front-ends from Virginia Diodes, and Xilinx RF-SoC ZCU-111 for DSP operations. A 1 GHz baseband example at 145.5 GHz is provided. The experiment uses horn antennas with 21 dB gain. The SNR is about 40 dB without cross correlation gain in the detector which provides an additional 15 dB in link margin. Real-time bit rate of 128 Mbps is achieved. Example applications include vehicle-to-vehicle, vehicle-to-infrastructure, backhaul, device-to-aerostat. This paper provides a platform from which further design work will lead to increased data rate and/or range, and enhance security through encryption. Future designs will facilitate digital interfaces, such as, ethernet, AXI, PCIe and USB-C.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Base Station Tightly Coupled Antenna Array Using Plastic Materials as Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel plastic antenna for outdoor 5G smart streetlight base station systems and operating in the Sub-6 GHz B42 band (3.4-3.6 GHz). The antenna assembly utilizes a PEI plastic material with added glass fiber as the substrate. In this system, the filter also employs the same material and shares a common backing board with the antenna. Simulations indicate that the antenna achieves a return loss of <-15 dB, isolation of <-20 dB, a maximum gain of 12 dBi within the 3.4-3.6 GHz frequency range. Additionally, the use of plastic materials results in a total weight of less than 2 kg.

articleTitle: Comparison and Validation of Different Tissue Mimicking Protocols for The Novel Development of an Arm Tissue Phantom
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Chronic skin wound monitoring affects over 10 million patients in the US and Europe annually, and the estimated cost for treatment is around $40 billion annually. As a result, our team has developed a sensor that monitors the stage and progress of burn wounds. Ideally, this sensor would be tested on actual burn tissue. However, there are intense regulatory and health issues to go through. Tissue Mimicking materials have been developed to bypass this issue. However, current phantom models are restricted to only one type of tissue. In this work, microwave tissue phantoms from seven different protocols will be examined to determine the most effective method to create a microwave tissue phantom that will replicate an entire human arm. Currently, inaccuracies in the results are being investigated to determine the protocols that will be used to develop the arm tissue phantom.

articleTitle: Broadband Delayed Border Oblique Incidence Simulation Technique for Finite Difference Time Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An FDTD technique that enables broadband simulation of periodic structures under oblique wave incidence is described. It is based on the asynchronous FDTD implementation intrinsic to the Hipercone HiFDTD code which uses space-temporal blocking for the mesh update. Within the delayed border technique, the full spectrum is obtained for a single angle of incidence in one simulation. The technique is benchmarked on the example of grating coupled plasmonic metamaterial where oblique incidence simulations are important for the predictions of the reflectance resonance shifts.

articleTitle: High-Bandwidth Aperture-Coupled 4×4 Patch Antenna Array at 28GHz for Thin Device Integration Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Millimeter wave (mmWave) communication systems have gained attention in addressing the capacity needs of future 5G and Next-G networks. The distinct features of the mm Wave signals, especially their ability to penetrate fog, rain, and clouds, enable applications like all-weather radar and sensing. Additionally, the broad bandwidth of the mmWave band makes it highly appealing for ultra high-speed wireless and satellite communications. Despite the promising bandwidth, mmWave frequencies greatly suffer from path loss, diffraction, blocking, rain attenuation, atmospheric absorption, and foliage loss behavior compared to microwave bands. Fortunately, the small wavelength of mmWave frequencies allows the deployment of multiple antenna elements in the same form factor, providing substantial spatial processing gain that can theoretically offset isotropic path losses. Nevertheless, the implementation of antenna array in the mmWaves is often computationally exhaustive in addition to implementation barriers that drastically affect the expected gains. Moreover, certain low-profile structures necessitated the use of thin substrates, causing an exponential decrease on antenna bandwidth.

articleTitle: Wideband Supercavity Operation of Combined HIR-SIW Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel integration of a high-index resonator (HIR) with substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) technology tailored for a wideband supercavity operation regime. An expanded supercavity region spanning approximately 1 GHz is identified adjacent to the bound states in the continuum (BIC) state. Through numerical optimization, coupling parameters between the HIR and SIW are fine-tuned to mitigate pass-band loss and elevate the Q-factor up to 350 in a miniaturized combined HIR-SIW resonator.

articleTitle: Object Classification using Electromagnetic Data and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We created a scatterer database based on the modified MNIST data set. Using simple neural networks, we achieve a 90% accuracy in classifying objects. We investigated the accuracy as a function of antenna number and data set size. For large data sets, neural networks exhibit a higher accuracy compared to other traditional machine learning methods.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Blade Antenna for Automotive Cellular Applications using Altair Feko
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Cellular networks, such as Long-Term Evolution (LTE) and 5G, have emerged as the primary mode of communication in automotive applications. To support the wide range of frequency bands used in these networks, the development of a compact and broadband antenna that can fit within the volume constraints of a roof-top (shark fin) antenna assembly is crucial. Utilizing a fast and precise optimization engine can facilitate the optimization of interactions between different antennas. We present the optimization of a C-Blade antenna with a C-shaped slot, which can cover a broad frequency band from 800 MHz to 5 GHz besides other application antennas. The optimization process involved using Altair Feko and the built-in optimizer GRSM (Global Response Surface Method) to ensure that the antenna met the performance specifications while adhering to size constraints. The Blade antenna's design and optimization were based on advanced electromagnetic simulations and included the consideration of various factors, such as impedance matching, radiation efficiency, and pattern characteristics.

articleTitle: An Interactive Visualization of Electrostatic Electric Field and Potential Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A MATLAB app for user display of electric field vectors and potential distribution due to electric charges is developed. The app increases the number of ways users can be engaged with and understand electrostatic fields. Point charges can be placed in a domain with adjustable coordinates and values using mouse clicking and dragging. The resultant electric potential strength distribution and electric field vectors from user defined charges can be displayed separately or together.
