articleTitle: 1-bit Wideband Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Design at Sub-6 Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a 1-bit wideband reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) design operating at sub-6 band is proposed. The unit cells of the RIS surface are designed based on a three-layer stacked patch structure. Employing a 1-bit PIN diode to reconfigure the phase states, a phase difference of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${180^0} \pm {20^0}$</tex> is observed over the frequency range of 4.81 –5.77 GHz, corresponding to a 19.2% fractional bandwidth. The reflection magnitude of the unit cell is above –3 dB in the band of interest, and the cross-polarization of the scattered waves is found significantly lower than the single-patch structure. The RIS array with a dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.\;2\lambda \times \;5.\;1\lambda$</tex>, corresponding to a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16\; \times \;10$</tex> array is structured according to the proposed unit cell with good beam steering capabilities.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Implementation for Material Characterization at W-Band Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Bandwidth requirements are continuously pushing radio frequency (RF) engineering designs to higher frequencies. In addition, knowledge of material characteristics, particularly the dielectric constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}})$</tex> and loss tangent (tano), is an important requirement for such design applications. Several method types exist for characterizing materials, but Transmission/Reflection (T/R) methods are the most suitable for determining characteristics over a range of frequencies. T/R methods place the material under test (MUT) within a transmission line and extract the dielectric constant from the S-parameters. The relationship between the dielectric constant and S-parameters is given by the Nicholson Ross-Weir (NRW) equation, which makes assumptions and approximations that often lead to inaccuracies, especially at higher frequencies.

articleTitle: Foldable Circularly Polarized Tightly Coupled Dipole Array for High Resolution Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A foldable wide band circularly polarized Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (CP- TCDA) is presented for high resolution spaceborne radars. For the first time, we propose a wideband circularly polarized array based on the TCDA concept. The design employs orthogonally placed dipoles, and incorporates strategically positioned capacitive pads. Orthogonally oriented dipoles are connected through inherently concentric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> phase shifters. Further, the array is highly conformal with the ground plane, placed at close proximity of the array plane. The array uses a combination of rigid and flexible substrates to adopt accordion-like folding. This foldable CP- TCDA provides an impedance bandwidth of VSWR < 3 from 103 MHz to 408 MHz, and an axial ratio of < 3 dB from 160 MHz to 320 MHz.

articleTitle: Development of a 3U CubeSat Electromagnetic Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Cube satellites (CubeSats) have become an increasingly approachable gateway for enthusiasts to access space at low-cost, with their versatility allowing for many functionalities to be implemented on one small platform. Of the various subsystems, the communication system is perhaps the most critical to mission success. As CubeSat size and complexity grows, it becomes increasingly important to characterize the im-pact of the structural elements of the CubeSat on the radiation properties of the communications antennas placed thereon. This is especially crucial during the Launch and Early Operations Phase (LEOP) when the CubeSat attempts to reach the desired stable orbit. By knowing the radiation patterns during different stages of deployment, such as the tumbling stage, the CubeSat design may be optimized to ensure a successful communication link between the ground station and the CubeSat. Furthermore, the impact of failure mechanisms during LEOP on the communication link may be studied, leading to the development of contingency plans.

articleTitle: Multilayer Reconfigurable Antenna Design for RADAR Sensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel, high-frequency, multilayer reconfigurable antenna with PIN diodes designed for radar sensor applications. The design, simulation, and implementation of multilayer configuration detailing integration of the bias circuit for a practical array configuration is given. The radiation fields for cross-polarization (XPR) and co-polarization have also been investigated. The proposed design operates effectively across a wide frequency range, spanning from 12 to 24 GHz, and demonstrates a peak gain of 7.36dB.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Nanophotonic and Radio-Frequency Devices using Fast Maxwell Solvers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Most electromagnetic devices arising from practical nanophotonic and radio-frequency (RF) applications require significant effort to model and design due to the lack of analytical solutions to Maxwell's equations for all but the simplest problems. Such systems usually require numerical simulation for analysis, but they often also pose serious challenges for electromagnetic simulation software due to being electrically large and/or having very fine features. The Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method often turns out to be the only practical approach when dealing with extremely large, such as silicon photonic devices or large arrays of antennas. Frequency-domain methods that utilize volumetric meshes, such as the Finite Element Method (FEM) and the Finite-Difference Frequency-Domain (FDFD) method, produce large linear systems which have spectral conditioning properties that scale very poorly as the problem size increases. In this talk, we will introduce a fast high-order 3D boundary integral equation (BIE) solver based on the Nystrom method, which we have used to efficiently simulate large devices in the frequency domain, including silicon photonic devices with semi-infinite input and output waveguides. We will discuss the most recent developments to our BIE solvers, including automated high-order meshing of planar structures, adaptive integration for automated error control, and a new way to launch one-directional modes in waveguides efficiently. Next, we will show how BIE-based solvers can be coupled with gradient-based optimization algorithms to inverse design high-performance nanophotonic devices, and we will derive the adjoint method for rapid computation of the objective function gradients in the context of boundary integral methods. Inverse design examples will be presented, including a 1:2 silicon photonic power splitter and a nonadiabatic taper.

articleTitle: FEKO Simulations of Ultra-Passive Radio Frequency Fresnel Rings Signal Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Through the New Mexico Small Business Assistance Program (NMSBA), Optical Radio Communications Technology (ORC Tech) has teamed up with Sandia National Laboratories (SNL) Engineers at the Sensors and Textiles Innovatively Tailored for Complex, High-Efficiency Detection (STITCHED) laboratory, to aid in the development and manufacturing of an ultra-passive, portable wireless signal amplification technology. This signal boosting technology was originally developed by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Johnson Space Center (JSC), as a collapsible, lightweight and portable signal-boosting device, in order to increase reception of weak signals encountered by astronaut crews on lunar missions. ORC Tech has licensed this technology from the NASA JSC with the intention to design specific prototypes for commercial industries, such as cellphones and other mobile devices.

articleTitle: Application of the Brillouin Diagram in Log-Periodic Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The utility of a Brillouin diagram for the design of a unit-cell and its translation to a log-periodic antenna from a uniform periodic (UP) array structure are discussed. Ten element UP array configurations of monopoles, folded monopoles (FM), folded inductively loaded monopoles (FILM), and folded normal mode helices (FNMH) are studied and the observations from said diagrams are utilized to determine critical parameters for achieving consistent backward radiation. The simulations show that initial configurations of FM and FILM log-periodic antennas without detailed parametric or optimization studies for a growth rate of 0.85 achieve VSWR < 2.5, expected radiation pattern, and acceptable front-to-back ratios over a large part of the HF band.

articleTitle: A Ratio-Norm Regularization for Sparsity-Promoting Electromagnetic Inversion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A nonlinear electromagnetic inversion method that promotes the sparsity in the model gradient is proposed for reconstruction of dielectric profiles. For regularization, the method uses the ratio of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{1}$</tex> -norm to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{2}$</tex> -norm (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{1}/l_{2}$</tex> -norm) which is a better approximation to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{0}$</tex> -norm than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{1}$</tex> -norm due to its scale-invariant property. To deal with the non-convexity of the resulting optimization problem, the alternating direction method of mul-tipliers is used to split the quotient structure of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{1}/l_{2}$</tex> -norm. Consequently, the optimization problem is separated into several sub-steps that are executed iteratively in an alternating fashion. Numerical results show that the proposed method produces more accurate reconstructions of spatially sparse dielectric profiles (by preserving edges and reducing artifacts) compared to the methods relying on Tikhonov and total variation regularization.

articleTitle: Novel PM-Assisted Three-Layer Sub-Harmonic Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a permanent magnet-assisted 3-layer sub-harmonic synchronous machine as a promising solution in the transportation sector. Through finite element analysis, the machine exhibits notable improvements over traditional machines, showcasing a 7.8% reduction in torque ripple and an 8.3% increase in average torque. Precise design parameters yield enhanced performance compared to five different synchronous machines. The incorporation of surface-mounted permanent magnets contributes to superior torque generation, making the machine a promising candidate for advancing in transportation applications.

articleTitle: AI-Based Multi-Objective Design Optimization Environment for EV Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This study introduces a characterization and design optimization environment suitable for Electric Vehicle Wireless Power Transfer charging systems. It utilizes a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) search algorithm and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), in conjunction with 3D EM Finite Element and State Space models to determine the optimal design parameters of wireless power transfer charging pads. The multi-objective optimization problem investigated considers system efficiency, output power, total material cost, and electromagnetic leakage.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic and Thermal Analysis of Silver-Based Low -Emissivity Coating Technology for Energy Saving Sustainable Windows Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Trends towards environmental sustainability have been driving the need for more efficient and energy saving buildings. Modern energy saving windows are now commonly used in buildings, and increasingly used in the transportation domain. They allow better insulation that is necessary to meet current regulations of energy performance. Recently, it was reported that up to 14% of typical commercial buildings can be due to overall cooling, heating, and ventilating systems while 30% of that wasted energy can be coming from the building's envelope. Energy waste through windows alone is estimated to cost U.S. consumers roughly ∃40 billion each year. Radiation losses occur through the window glass and represent about 60% of the total heat loss in a standard window. Thus, the need for controlling and maintaining the heat transfer via these windows is becoming critical.

articleTitle: Tucker-SVD-FFT-Accelerated Solution of Volume Integral Equation for Magneto-Quasi-Static Analysis of Voxelized Geometries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A Tucker decomposition-singular value decomposition (SVD)-fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based acceleration scheme, called Tucker-SVD-Fft, is proposed for rapidly solving volume integral equation (VIE) for magneto-quasi-static (MQS) analysis of voxelized geometries. The proposed acceleration scheme uses Tucker, SVD, and FFT acceleration techniques to perform matrix-vector multiplications related to far, nearby, and self interactions of the voxel groups, respectively. The resulting Tucker-SVD- FFT-accelerated VIE solver is applicable to multiscale and non-uniformly discretized voxelized geometries, unlike its pure FFT - accelerated counterpart. Preliminary results demonstrate that the Tucker compression yields at least one order of magnitude better compression compared to SVD compression, while the proposed acceleration scheme outperforms the FFT and SVD acceleration schemes for MQS analysis of a uniformly voxelized and well-seperated structure. While the scheme's application to the MQS analysis is demonstrated here, its adoption to the full-wave analysis is underway.

articleTitle: Inverse Design Techniques for Optimizing Passive Lumped Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The recent advancements in Microwave Integrated Circuits (MICs) have demonstrated that an interdigital capacitor (IDCap) can be designed to achieve a significantly enhanced quality factor to bandwidth ratio when compared to a lumped capacitor (N.L.K. Ngugen, et al., “A 1-160 GHz InP distributed amplifier using 3-D interdigital capacitors,” IEEE Microw. Wirel. Compon. Lett., May 2020). In this work, the IDCap was designed to mimic the impedance response of a lumped capacitor across the frequency band of 230− 240 MHz. Various global and local optimization techniques, including the genetic algorithm (GA), mixedinteger sequential quadratic programming (MISAP), and gradient descent (GD), were employed to attain an optimal IDCap design.

articleTitle: Advanced Radar Coverage Simulations Using WRAP in Altair Feko
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Radar Coverage Calculations can range from basic Line-of-Sight (LoS) Visibility to more complex calculations, under different propagation conditions. The parameters of interest are Radio Optical LoS, heights at which targets of certain Radar Cross Section (RCS) can be detected with certain probability, RCS size at which targets at specified heights can be detected with certain probability, and impact of jammers and obstructions on radar coverage. In this paper, a case study is presented using the WRAP module of Altair Feko with multiple, relevant propagation models, to inform user of the relevant capabilities of WRAP, which are used by commercial organizations to make informed decisions.

articleTitle: A Subgrid Model Utilizing Extra- and Inter-polation Schemes for the Nonstandard FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The use subgridding in the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method can significantly reduce the overall computational burden. This is particularly applicable in the scattering analysis of electrically-large objects with partially fine structures or dielectrics, such as aircrafts or ships. In this paper, we propose a 3D subgrid model for the nonstandard (NS) FDTD method via simple extra- and inter-polation schemes for efficient grid connection. Also, a perfectly matched absorber is employed to mitigate long-time instabilities. Numerical results verify that the proposed model exhibits high accuracy even in its simple form; it has sufficient stability and low system costs.

articleTitle: Analytic Integrals with $\nabla\partial R^{-1}/\partial n$ Kernels for Linear Triangular Mesh Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Analytic expressions are presented for surface integrals whose kernels are the gradient of the normal derivative of the static Green's function. The derived integrals are valid over linear triangular mesh elements for constant and linear basis functions. Numerical results are validated in double precision using an arbitrary-precision math library. Near-machine precision accuracy is achieved for the cases presented.

articleTitle: Aperture Taper Efficiency and Directivity – A Comparison of Results Using Analytical Techniques and Computer Simulations Using FEKO
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The directivity of an aperture antenna having a uniformly distributed electric field may be estimated from the formula.

articleTitle: A Mixed-Order Divergence-Conforming Locally Corrected Nystrom Method for Triangular Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A locally corrected Nystrom method is presented that better models a mixed-order, divergence-conforming space on triangular cells. The theory is developed for a space that is complete to the same order for both the unknown quantity and its divergence. The method is implemented for the electric field integral equation, and convergence results are presented for scattering from a perfectly conducting sphere.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Rough Surface Profiles using a CNN-enhanced RTM-based Inversion Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Numerical methods that can accurately reconstruct rough surface profiles are used in various fields of engineering such as remote sensing, microwave imaging, optics, nondestructive testing, etc. These methods express the electromagnetic scattered fields measured away from the surface itself as an integral function of the surface profile. This mapping is highly nonlinear and ill-posed (D. Colton and R. Kress, 1998, SpringerVerlag, Berlin), and therefore its inversion for reconstruction of the surface profile from measured scattered fields is challenging. This inversion can done using semi-analytic asymptotic approaches such as the small perturbation and the Rytov approximation methods (A.G. Voronovich, 2013, Springer-Verlag, Berlin), however the range of applicability of these approaches is rather limited. Fully numerical methods that rely on Newton-type iterative linearization techniques and regularization schemes such as those in (S. Arhab, et al., PIERS, pp. 3495–3500, 2017) and (A. Sefer, A. Yapar, IEEE Trans. Geosci Remote Sens., vol. 59, pp. 1041–1051, 2021) have a wider range of applicability but they suffer from convergence and accuracy issues.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of Coil and its Pulse Generator for Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Experiments in Mice
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) is a non-invasive method for studying and treat brain-related ailments. This approach uses coils driven by high-current pulses that in turn generate electric fields in the brain. To better understand TMS, researchers study its effects on small animals like mice. We present an efficient design of mouse coils along with power drivers for TMS mouse experiments.

articleTitle: A Scalable Multi-Physics Simulation of Dancing Ferrofluid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We propose a rapid and scalable method for performing multi-physics simulations of magnetized ferrofluids. A key contribution of our method is the simulation of magnetic phenomena from a kinetic statistical physics perspective, through the use of the Lattice Boltzmann Method. This approach provides a unified numerical framework, seamlessly integrating a two-phase fluid solver with considerations for surface tension and a magnetic field solver to account for the Helmholtz force. Compared to existing literature, the work shows good performance on scalability and parallelism.

articleTitle: Design of a Tunable 2-bit Phase Shifter at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: With the emergence of fifth-generation (5G) communication, millimeter-wave (mmWave) radio frequency (RF) systems have attracted much attention for their ability to support higher data rates and much wider bandwidths. Major challenges at mmWave frequencies are high atmospheric attenuation, signal path loss, and unwanted interference, leading to a low quality of service. These challenges can be overcome using high-gain phased antenna arrays with beamforming capabilities. However, traditional beamsteering systems use phase shifters and are mostly suited for narrowband operation with inherently high-power requirements. For wider band operation, these beamformers require complex, lossy, and bulky components. Alternatively, frequency reconfigurable and tunable phase shifters have emerged as a promising solution to achieve wide spectral and spatial diversity with minimal hardware complexity and losses.

articleTitle: Superior Far Field Accuracy of the Normally-Integrated MFIE Compared to the Conventional MFIE for Flat-faceted Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The accuracy of numerical results obtained from the normally-integrated MFIE formulation is compared to the conventional MFIE for flat-faceted targets and Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions. The NIMFIE approach appears to be less sensitive to fictitious surface discontinuities due to faceted models and consequently provides more accurate bistatic scattering cross section than the MFIE. The NIMFIE formulation is free from internal resonances and for these targets usually outperforms the combined-field integral equation for far field accuracy.

articleTitle: Fresnel Region Fields of Aperture Antennas Used in EMC Radiated Emission Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: MIL-STD-461G RE102 specifics limits for radiated electric field emissions from military ground, ships, submarines, and aircraft. Additionally, MIL-STD-464D, defines the required electromagnetic environment for testing system venerability. Testing is conducted over the range of frequencies from 2 MHz to 18 G Hz and typical antennas used to cover this range of frequencies include an active vertical dipole, a Bicone, and the double ridge guide horn. Pyramidal horn antennas used to generate a required electromagnetic environment (per MIL-STD-464D) are often positioned near the test system and consequently in the near field or Fresnel region of the radiator. Our group is undertaking a broad based experimental and numerical study to better understand the nature of the near field radiation characteristics of aperture antennas and this paper shall provide a summary of our accomplishments to date. Our results demonstrate that the near field gain of a smaller aperture antenna may be larger than that of a larger aperture antenna. This simple fact can be overlooked by practicing EMI test engineers who are accustomed to choosing a higher gain horn to generate a larger electric field.

articleTitle: Design and Finite-Difference Time-Domain Analysis of Three-Dimensional Printed W - Band Reflector Fresnel Lens Antenna Using Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene Plastic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Herein, we present the design and analysis of two three-dimensional printed W -band reflector Fresnel lens antennas with different diameters, using acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) plastic, based on the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. Initially, lenses with 150 and 250 mm diameters were designed, incorporating the Fresnel lens structure to reduce the thickness and mitigate the gain degradation due to the high dielectric loss of ABS plastic. Subsequent analysis using the FDTD method revealed maximum antenna gains of 33.3 and 37.6 dBi for the 150- and 250-mm lens, respectively, demonstrating a gain increase of 4.3 dB with a 2.8-fold increase in aperture size.

articleTitle: Scalable Parallel Implementation of the Broadband Delayed Border Oblique Incidence Simulation Technique for FDTD
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: With the development of modern high-performance approaches in the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) electromagnetic simulations (e.g. EmpireXPU, Tidy3D, HiFDTD) the routine cloud-based computations become an attractive solution for the end user. When properly scaled, these simulations may utilize the computational power otherwise unavailable locally, resulting in tremendous decrease of the simulation times and compute performance reaching hundreds of billions Yee cells per second.

articleTitle: Modern Radar Vertical Coverage Diagram Including Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Radar vertical coverage diagrams are created using either spreadsheets or custom code. These diagrams are used by radar designers and are based on theoretical calculations of the radar range equation. A new method that includes RF impairments and DSP signal processing design aspects is proposed. A phased array with a cosecant square beam pattern is used to validate the new method in a pulsed radar. The method is then augmented to include interference (e.g. jamming).

articleTitle: Low-Loss Ultra-Wideband Feeding Network for Foldable Spaceborne Multifunctional Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: There is a growing interest for multifunctional spaceborne apertures that simultaneously perform tasks such as remote sensing, communications, and meteorology. To this end, ultra-wideband antenna arrays have been designed to provide for large bandwidths of over 46: 1, operating from VHF to millimeter wave frequencies (A. D. Johnson, J. Zhong, S. B. Venkatakrishnan, E. A. Alwan and J. L. Volakis, “Phased Array with Low-Angle Scanning and 46: 1 Bandwidth,” IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, vol. 68, no. 12, pp. 7833–7841, Dec. 2020). However, for small satellites, there is also a requirement for folding/packing. For the latter, the feed must also be foldable and packable. As such, for an array of several elements, individual coaxial feeding may not be attractive as they cause congestion, add weight, and limit deployability.

articleTitle: Simulation of Mutual Coupling in Aperiodic Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Aperiodic antenna arrays improve the bandwidth of the array but are more computationally expensive to simulate and optimize. The method shown here reduces the complexity of simulating array coupling effects by considering a smaller sphere of influence surrounding each element. Results are presented comparing the coupled simulation with the isolated element simulation.

articleTitle: Three- Dimensional Synthetic Aperture Radar Image Formation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Three-dimensional Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery reveals information about the scene in the range, azimuth, and elevation directions and is far more discernable than two-dimensional imagery. The information in the added dimension gives more details and insight into the size, shape, and orientation of objects within a scene. It can also solve some of the imaging issues found in two-dimensional imagery, such as layover [1], [2]. The paper begins with an overview of the history and development of three-dimensional SAR imaging. This is followed by the development of the three-dimensional polar format algorithm. The linear trace version of the Fourier slice theorem is given along with the derivation of the three-dimensional backprojection algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of Pentaband Antenna with High Frequency Ratio for CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A circular polarized (CP) pentaband antenna based on the aperture-in-aperture (AIA) concept is presented for CubeSat applications. This AIA consists of five different bands ranging from L-band to Ka-band. Four antennas, each operating at a specific frequency band, namely 12 GHz, 18.5 GHz, 26 GHz, and 32 GHz, are incorporated into an L-band (1.5 GHz) antenna. Notably, the five antennas can operate simultaneously for a CubeSat downlink operation. More in detail, four square-shaped slots were etched in the L-band antenna to fit four different band antennas. The maximum to minimum frequency ratio for this shared aperture is around 21.3. The antenna shows a realized gain of 5 – 10 dBic with good CP bandwidth (< 3 dB) for the operational frequency range. The realized gain of L-band, X-band, K-bandl, and K-band2 are 5.05 dBi, 7.8 dBi, 7.1 dBi, and 7.97 dBi at 1.5, 12.5, 18.5, and 26 GHz, respectively. The realized gain of the Ka-band antenna is 9.97 dBi at 32 GHz. The simulation data shows that this antenna can be a great candidate for multi-frequency operation of CubeSat antenna.

articleTitle: Characterization and Comparative Analysis of the Electrostatic Properties of Different Lunar Regolith Simulants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In pursuing sustainable lunar exploration and habitation, understanding the electrostatic and electromagnetic behavior of lunar dust and regolith particles is receiving significant interest. However, the limited number of lunar regolith samples collected during the Apollo missions is insufficient to sustain the large number of current lunar experimental studies. Therefore, many lunar simulants have been fabricated using terrestrial materials to emulate the properties of lunar dust and regolith particles. Different lunar regolith simulants are used to represent different moon regions and for different applications. In this work, we study the electrostatic properties of the particles of two lunar simulants: JSC-l A and NU - LHT-4 M. JSC-lA is a simulant for the lunar mare regions, the dark areas of the moon, whereas NU-LHT-4M is a highland simulant, the lighter or brighter parts of the moon. Both simulants have particles with stable 3D shapes and have been used in a wide range of experiments. Utilizing advanced 3D X-ray tomography, we imaged the 3D particle shapes of thousands of particles from each simulant with sub-micron resolution. Using the open-source SCUFF-EM package, a Method of Moments (MOM)-based tool, we calculated the electrostatic polarizability tensors of the particles in each simulant. The particles were assigned a relative dielectric permittivity of 9.8 following: Grant Heiken, David Vaniman, and Bevan M. French, Lunar sourcebook: A user's guide to the Moon, No. 1259, Cup Archive, 1991. The electrostatic polarizability describes the electric dipole moment acquired by the particle when exposed to electric fields of different directions. After calculating the polarizability tensor, its eigenvalues are calculated and arranged in decreasing order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{1}\geq P_{2}$</tex> 2: P3. Our quantitative analysis shows significant differences between the polarizability values of the NU-LHT-4M and JSC-IA simulants. Averaging 5000 particles from each simulant, NU-LHT-4M yielded average polarizability values <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P_{1}=240,527,\ P_{2}=169,075,\ P_{3}=111,707)$</tex> whereas the average JSC I-A values were <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P_{1}=127,243,\ P_{2}=93,879,\ P_{3}=69,671)$</tex>. Comparisons with previously published polarizability results from actual lunar regolith particles collected in the Apollo missions will be presented.

articleTitle: A Magnetic Window Antenna Based on Artificial Electromagnetic Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The problem of the communication blackout when aircraft passing through the atmosphere is still worth further study. Based on the artificial electromagnetic structure which can excite the near-field magnetic field, a novel righthand circularly polarized magnetic window antenna is proposed. In the case of 0.5 T magnetic field, the attenuation is reduced to 14.0 dB through the plasma with a density magnitude of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. The results show that this approach can significantly improve the communication effectiveness when encountering the blackout caused by the plasma.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Perfectly-Matched Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Inverse design has been applied to a variety of complex electromagnetic structures including multifunctional and multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) devices, where analytical design methods are limiting. We have previously reported on the inverse design of single-input, single-output Perfectly-Matched Metamaterials (PMMs). PMMs are inhomogeneous, anisotropic 2D metamaterials composed of unit cells that remain impedance-matched to each other and the surroundings under all excitations. PMMs rely primarily on refractive effects and exhibit broadband operation. This work presents the inverse design of a compact MIMO device based on PMMs: a 2D beamformer with prescribed amplitude and phase profiles that exhibits zero scan loss.

articleTitle: Compact Multibeam Antenna Without Crossovers Based on FCSIW for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: With the improvement of millimeter wave (mm-wave) technology, the future mm-wave antenna is developing in the direction of miniaturization. In this paper, a compact mm-wave multibeam antenna based on Folded C-Type substrate integrated waveguide (FCSIW) without crossovers is proposed. the multibeam array antenna comprise a conventional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> butler matrix (BM) and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> slot array antenna base on FCSIW. The size of the final multibeam array antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.9\lambda_{0}\times 7.6\lambda 0$</tex>, which is reduced by 30% compared with the conventional multibeam antenna based on FCSIW. The proposed antenna will be one of the very attractive candidates for 5G mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: Towards Quantifying the Effect of Material Uncertainty on RCS Predictions of Composite Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A Monte Carlo analysis is performed to study the sensitivity of the mono static radar cross section (RCS) of thin-plate targets in the Austin RCS Benchmark Suite, which are shown to have high sensitivity to small variations in the material parameters. The RCS of the targets are found numerically for each material sample and the computational costs are reported. The case studies show that quantifying the impact of material uncertainty on the RCS (1) for a homogenous target model is not sufficient to quantify the impact of material uncertainty for a composite target model containing the same material, even if the other materials have no accompanying uncertainty, and (2) requires the use of fast methods even for electromagnetically small composite target models.

articleTitle: Method for Analytically Finding the Left and Right Nullspace of Curl-Curl Operator in Unsymmetrical Finite-Difference Subgridding Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The nullspace of a curl-curl operator is of critical importance to the efficient and accurate broadband solution of Maxwell's equations. In this paper, we develop an analytical method to generate the left and right nullspace of the curlcurl operator for unsymmetrical finite-difference subgridding algorithms. The nullspaces are generated analytically from the mesh information without the need for numerical computation. The method is applicable to an arbitrary base grid and sub-grid configuration. Comparisons with a brute-force eigenvalue solution for finding nullspaces have demonstrated the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method. The method has also been successfully applied to solving the low-frequency breakdown problem of full wave finite-difference solvers.

articleTitle: Bidomain Boundary Element Modeling of Pseudo-Realistic Neurons with Advanced Membrane Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Brain cells known as neurons transmit electrical signals by controlling the transport of chemical ions across their membrane. The presence of an electric (E-) field generated by an external device modulates these brain signals, producing therapeutic effects. Electrodes and coil technologies have been developed to use E-fields to treat psychiatric disorders, smoking addiction, and tremors from Parkinson's disease.

articleTitle: Algorithmic Acceleration of the Chebyshev-based Boundary Integral Equation Method for 3D Maxwell Problems using the Interpolated Factored Green Function
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A predominant majority of electromagnetic devices required for modern applications in today's society, such as high-speed wireless communications and integrated photonics, are difficult to model due to lack of analytical solutions, requiring full-wave numerical solution of Maxwell's equations. Popular numerical approaches for solving Maxwell's equations computationally include finite-difference, finite element, and boundary integral equation methods. Finite-difference and finite element methods, which are volumetric approaches, are often limited to being used for solving small to moderately sized problems due to resulting in prohibitively large and poorly conditioned linear systems. Boundary integral equation (BIE) methods, on the other hand, only require meshing and solving for unknowns on the surfaces between objects of different materials and can result in systems of equations with significantly fewer unknowns, especially in scenarios with high volume-to-surface area ratios. However, it is well known that BIE methods result in dense, rather than sparse, linear systems, which require <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{N}^{2})$</tex> operations to solve iteratively when conditioned well or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{N}^{3})$</tex> to solve using dense linear algebra solvers, such as LU decomposition. Fortunately, numerous algorithmic acceleration approaches exist (e.g., FMM, Butterfly, AIM), but they are either specialized for low-frequency problems or require Fast Fourier Transforms (FFTs), which are challenging to parallelize effectively and limit their scaling to very large problems. The Interpolated Factored Green's Function (IFGF) was recently introduced for acoustic scattering [JCP 2021, Bauinger and Bruno] as an alternative algorithmic acceleration approach which also achieves O(N log N) computational complexity but can be parallelized very effectively due to relying on nested polynomial interpolation rather than on FFTs for propagating information from sources to targets. The IFGF works equally well for low and high-frequency problems and does not require different treatment for the high-frequency regime. The IFGF method works by factoring out a “centered factor” from the Green function kernel, which does not depend on the source coordinates and makes the resulting kernel (referred to as the “analytic factor”) easy to interpolate with high accuracy over directional cone structures by using low-order polynomial interpolants. On its own, this interpolation approach can achieve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{N}^{3/2})$</tex> time complexity in the best-case scenario; however, similar to multi-level approaches such as the MLFMM, this can be brought down to O(N log N) by producing an octree of boxes and leveraging nested interpolation to reuse interpolants produced at lower (smaller boxes) levels for the higher ones. In this work, we extend the IFGF method for the first time to the fully vectorial 3D Maxwell case. We will begin by introducing the general IFGF method, followed by covering details associated with its extension to Maxwell problems. Examples will be presented for dielectric scattering problems using the well-conditioned N-Müller formulation and timing data will be shown that confirms the O(N log N) computational complexity of the approach.

articleTitle: Towards the Design of a Non-invasive Glucose Monitoring Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The development of noninvasive glucose sensors is a technology that can improve the lives of people with diabetes. Their design is a very challenging electromagnetic measurement problem as electromagnetic (EM) fields are used to penetrate the skin and varying concentrations of glucose modify the permittivity of the ensemble of human tissue. The objective of this work is to measure the changes in glucose levels via the shift in permittivity by using an antenna placed on the body. Our antenna has been designed to be placed on the skin in the upper shoulder area. Using electromagnetic simulations of frequency dependent material, we have designed the antenna sensor to detect a change in relative permittivity up to ± 15%. These results are also confirmed with measurements on a human shoulder.

articleTitle: Lumped-Element Circuit Construction for Lossy Distributed Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: It has been observed that it is possible to construct a lumped-element circuit model for distributed lossless circuits using an admittance power matching (APM) method with an augmented electric field integral equation (AEFIE). This presentation describes a similar procedure for lossy circuits modeled using an augmented electric field volume integral equation (AEVIE) formulation. Two significant modifications of the APM procedure previously applied to the AEFIE are required to reliably construct physically meaningful, lumped-element circuits from an AEVIE formulation of a lossy distributed circuit. These modifications are summarized, and numerical results illustrate the performance of the resulting procedure.

articleTitle: 1D Equivalent Circuit Models for Computation of the Dispersion Relation of 2D Metamaterial-based EBG Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Electromagnetic bandgap structures (EBGs) are useful at suppressing guided wave propagation for certain frequency bands and for certain directions of propagation. They have found many applications, such as surface wave suppression for reduction of mutual coupling in patch antenna arrays (A. Lamminen et al., “UC-EBG on LTCC for 60-GHz Frequency Band Antenna Applications,” IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, Vol. 57, No. 10, 2904-2912, October 2009), among others. These planar EBGs are often analyzed by extracting their full 2D dispersion relation using a full-wave electromagnetic solver such as the Ansys HFSS Eigenmode solver. This process, though accurate, is computationally intensive and often takes several hours to complete. Hence, equivalent circuit models based on transmission-line theory are needed for fast extraction of the dispersion relation, allowing for efficient EBG design for a given application.

articleTitle: A Novel A -ϕ Formulation for Efficient Electromagnetic Computations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In numerical simulation of electromagnetic problems, potential-based formulations have advantages over field-based formulations because of their immunity to the low-frequency breakdown catastrophe. Recently, an all-frequency stable formulation has been proposed to solve electromagnetic problems in a wide frequency band. This formulation employs magnetic vector and electric scalar potentials, as well as an auxiliary potential to enforce an inhomogeneous Coulomb gauge. However, such a three-potential formulation has encountered convergence issues at low frequencies. To avoid the convergence issue and improve computational efficiency, a novel formulation with only two potentials and an implicit Coulomb gauge is proposed in this paper. A numerical example is presented to show its solution accuracy and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Model for a Waveguide Fed Dual Rectangular Slot Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An equivalent circuit is used to model a waveguide fed dual rectangular slot antenna to understand the slot resonance and mutual coupling effect between two slots. The circuit models including LC circuit, waveguide section, parallel RLC combination, and transformer are introduced to describe the scattering behaviors of each single slot. The mutual coupling effect acts like an absorptive band-stop filter which can be modeled as shorted serial RLC combination. Reflection response <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex> are analyzed in terms of the circuit parameters. The results obtained from the equivalent circuits are validated by the scattering parameters and current distribution using HFSS simulation, and exhibit good agreement over the frequency band of interest.

articleTitle: Gain Analysis of Domino and Tetromino-shaped Irregular Tiled Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Irregular array technique has gotten lots of attention for dramatically reducing T/R modules while maintaining high gain. However, the gain of irregular arrays decreases rapidly with scanning angles in practical designs. It is essential to determine the gain limits of irregular arrays across various angles. By introducing the concept of relative wave path difference (RWPD), we estimate the upper limits of irregular arrays using linear programming. For domino-shaped irregular arrays (two elements per subarray), the current results are close to the theoretical limits. However, for tetromino-shaped irregular arrays (four elements per sub array), it is expected that scanning gains can be further improved with advanced optimization tools and increased design flexibility.

articleTitle: Computing Derivatives of Finite Element Solutions by Automatic Derivative Programs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The derivatives of EM responses with respect to the design variables play a crucial role for gradient-based optimizations and sensitivity analysis. This paper focuses on computing the derivatives of EM responses solved using the finite element method (FEM). The primary challenge in obtaining derivatives of FEM solutions lies in determining the differential of the FEM governing equation's residuals. In this study, we employ the automatic derivative (AD) functions available in the PyTorch library to calculate the differentials. By utilizing the explicit expression of the FEM stiffness matrix and excitation vector, the AD tool efficiently computes the differentials of residuals with minimal computational effort, eliminating the need for manual differential calculations. The efficiency and accuracy of this method is validated through an example involving the calculation of the derivative of scattering matrix for a 2D dielectric cylinder scattering problem.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Radial Lines of an LP-RLSA for 40-50 GHz Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This study investigates the design of radial lines at four different geometric positions of a slot antenna using in a high frequency range of 40–50 GHz. The slot arrays were positioned in such a way that linear polarization was found with a broadside radiation pattern. The radial line dimensions were optimized to extract the best outcomes from the setup. A peak gain of 11.14 dB was achieved at 47.5 GHz and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> parameter reached as low as -46.06 dB. These radial lines provide an accurate prediction of what to expect when they are implemented to form a linearly polarized RLSA antenna.

articleTitle: Broadband Modeling of Mutual Coupling Between Surface-Mounted Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is a fundamental challenge in electronic systems. The use of filter structures, in-cluding surface-mounted (SMT) passive components, is essential to ensure the reliable operation of such systems. However, these devices are susceptible to parasitic coupling effects when placed in close proximity, leading to changes in their electromagnetic (EM) behaviour and potential EMI problems at a particular frequency range. This paper investigates the effects of different package sizes and placements on the EM coupling between devices using 3D fullwave finite element (FE) simulations and experimental measurements. Finally, an equivalent circuit model is derived from the FE simulation results that can be used in computationally more expensive EM-Co system simulations to account for these coupling mechanisms.

articleTitle: A Multi-Region ACA-Accelerated Approach for High-Quality-Factor Resonant Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Metallic cavities are used to protect internal electronic circuits against undesired external electromagnetic (EM) interactions. However, there might exist imperfect mechanical seams or joints on the structure through which the EM energy can couple and severely harm electronic circuits, especially when the cavity has high quality factors. To model such cavity problems at Sandia National Laboratories, we use Gemma, a frequency-domain linear electromagnetic code, which uses the method of moments to solve the EM surface integral equations on the exterior and the interior of the cavity and employs a narrow-slot sub-cell model to capture EM penetration through the slots. The cavity interior is coupled only through the slots, i.e. no direct interactions take place between the exterior and the interior. Since application of the moment method here gives a dense linear system, when iterative solutions are used, the memory requirements and computational cost are of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N^{2})$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> is the number of unknowns. This cost suggests the use of fast numerical techniques to reduce this complexity as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> grows. Compared with other fast techniques, the adaptive cross approximation (ACA) has the advantage of its purely algebraic nature, where the rank deficiency of well-separated matrix blocks is exploited. However, when applied directly to the entire cavity structure, the ACA fails to efficiently take advantage of the matrix sub-blocks that are partly made up of the zero interactions between the exterior and the interior.

articleTitle: Geometric Dispersion Effects of Sinusoidal Corrugation Depth and Periodicity in Coaxial Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Eigenmode studies for three classes of periodic coaxial cable transmission lines are examined. Specific conductor geometries include: (a) smooth inner, corrugated outer, (b) smooth outer, corrugated inner, and (c) corrugated inner, corrugated outer. Geometric dispersion, specifically linear and cubic phase advance coefficients, are tabulated to show general trends with corrugation depth and periodicity.

articleTitle: Recent Advancements in D-TTIT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A brief history of the development of the Discrete Taylor Transform and Inverse Transform (D-TTIT) is followed by new insights which are encapsulated in three Theorems. In one dimension (1D) the required inverses of the matrices can be calculated simply-by-inspection. It is shown that this enabling property remains valid in 2D and 3D versions of D-TTIT, by utilizing matrix tensor products, which “naturally” arise in the formulation. Application areas include finite difference method, optimization, and where high-order difference formulae are needed on uniform or nonuniform grids.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Simulation Method for Electromagnetic Scattering by Electrically Large Rough Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid simulation method for electromagnetic scattering by two-dimensional electrically large rough surfaces. Firstly, the beam simulation method (BSM) is used to divide the large-scale illumination area into several small-scale sub-regions. Since the Gaussian window of each sub-beam suppresses the illumination energy at the edges of each sub-region, the interaction between the sub-beams can be ignored, and these sub-regions can be solved individually. Secondly, the characteristics basis function method (CBFM) divides each sub-region into some sub-blocks, and the induced currents of each sub-block is expanded using the global feature basis functions (CBFs). And a reduction matrix for expansion coefficients of CBFs is constructed to reduce computational complexity. The comparison with method of moments (MoM) validates the new algorithm. In addition, the comparison with other fast methods indicates that the proposed hybrid algorithm has significant advantages in CPU time and memory storage.

articleTitle: Analytic Two-Dimensional Logarithm Integrals on Curvilinear Domains
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Analytic expressions are presented for two-dimensional integrals over curvilinear domains whose integrands are the product of a logarithmic kernel and a polynomial. Limitations of the expressions are discussed. Numerical results are validated in double precision using an arbitrary-precision math library [1]. Near-machine precision accuracy is achieved in many cases.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable HoneyComb Series Fed Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper proposes a reconfigurable honeycomb shape two-element antenna array for S-band (2.4-2.45 GHz). The substrate is placed on a hexagonal-shaped 3D-printed base. The authors previously proposed a foldable mechanism to reconfigure this array mechanically. In this paper, we propose an additional pattern reconfigurability electronically via phase-controlled feed.

articleTitle: All-in-One Integrated Multiport Receiver for Giga-Speed Backhaul Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a new millimeter wave (mm-wave) front-end receiver composed of a high gain antenna array integrated with a low-cost six-port receiver is demonstrated for mm-wave backhaul networks. As a direct down-convertor, a six-port circuit composed of some passive elements is implemented to ensure the acquisition of demodulated high-speed signals with acceptable bit error rates across the entire unlicensed 60-GHz bandwidth and various modulation schemes. Using the bonding wire interconnection technology and MHMIC technology, the antenna array is integrated into a compact package alongside the low noise amplifier and the six-port receiver.

articleTitle: Intelligent Geometric Alignment and Dimensions-Guided Approach for Design Optimization for Efficiency Improvement of WPT Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The essential detection of the secondary-side coil in wireless power transfer systems (WPTSs) for electric vehicles (EVs) is to ascertain the vehicle's effective charging zone. We propose design considerations for two prevalent coil types, ring, and spiral circular coils, which are widely used in WPTSs. A comprehensive analytical estimation of inductive characteristics for WPT is provided, followed by design optimization of the WPT system based on coil geometrical parameters and relative placement. To validate the theoretical analysis, COMSOL software is utilized to accurately determine the inductive parameters for our proposed 500W charging coils. Furthermore, we investigate the coupling coefficients of various coreless and cored charging pads with different geometric dimensions and coil alignments, recommending using an I-core to avoid bifurcation phenomena.

articleTitle: MFIE- Induced RCS Errors in CFIE Simulations of a Fan-Loaded Camera Box
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The smallest target in problem set IIIS-D of the Austin RCS Benchmark Suite—a fan-loaded cylindrical void in a camera box—is used to demonstrate the limited but significant impact of the errors in the classical solution of the combined-field integral formulation (CFIE). While almost all of the radar cross section (RCS) samples computed from the CFIE solution agree well with reference measurement data, at one frequency and one polarization the monostatic RCS samples over a small sector of angles aware of the void are found to (i) deviate significantly from the reference data and (ii) improve only marginally as the mesh is refined uniformly. The RCS errors are shown to arise from the magnetic-field IE contribution and the presence of a small gap in between the fan and the back wall of the void.

articleTitle: A Quantum-inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Beampattern Synthesis in Multi-User MIMO
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel methodology for array synthesis in multi-user MIMO systems. Utilizing binary variables to represent antenna excitation states, we encode desired beampattern properties, such as a narrow main lobe, low peak sidelobe level, and minimized inter-user interference, into a quadratic objective function. The optimal array excitation profile is then obtained through a quantum-inspired simulated bifurcation algorithm. Large-scale numerical experiments are performed to validate the performance of our method.

articleTitle: Modeling Two-Dimensional Material-Based Photodetectors with Finite-Difference Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We developed a finite-difference frequency-domain (FDFD) and a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) drift-diffusion equations solver that takes the multilayered background into account for realistic characterization. Comparisons between the numerical results and experiments validate the accuracy of the proposed approach in calculating the output current, quantum efficiency, and phase noise of the photodetector as a function of incident wavelength.

articleTitle: Numerical Accuracy and Airbox Size: A Comparison of FEM to MoM and Analytical Results for Dipole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: When simulating antenna problems using the finite element method (FEM), it is necessary to truncate the three-dimensional open region surrounding the antenna (so-called airbox), and apply boundary conditions at the edge of the computational domain such that the problem resembles that of radiation into free space. Generally, it is advised that the distance between a radiating surface and the simulation boundary be some minimum fraction of a wavelength, depending on the type of boundary condition being used. While per-forming FEM simulations of electrically small antennas, we found that the radiation pattern and efficiency can vary significantly with airbox size, even when this size met or exceeded the recommended minimum, and even when a very fine mesh density was maintained in the vicinity of the antenna. Further investigation has shown that this is the case for conventional antennas as well.

articleTitle: Effect of Rough Sea Surfaces on Hertzian Dipole Patterns in the HF Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Impact of realistic ocean surfaces on performance of a vertical Hertzian electric dipole in 3–30 MHz range is studied using Altair FEKO. MATLAB is used to generate the geometry of various ocean surfaces based on the Elfouhaily spectrum to best examine dependence on wind speed and direction. The rough sea surfaces are modeled as perfect electric conductors with a cosine taper merging into an infinite flat ocean modeled using Sommerfeld integrals. The affected radiation pattern of antenna pertaining to Beaufort sea states of 0, 2, 4, and 5 is then analyzed in the context of long range skywave propagation.

articleTitle: Simulation Studies of Electromagnetic Energy Absorption by Hydride Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper investigates the key parameters that contribute to electromagnetic (EM) energy absorption and heating of hydride materials which could be used to release hydrogen for use as a fuel. Our simulation study using COMSOL focuses on EM energy absorption and resulting temperature rise in a thin circular slab of hydride material using resonant dipole and loop antennas. Presented results delineate the effects of conductivity, relative permeability, antenna type and slab size on temperature rise when the distance and amount of RF power are kept fixed.

articleTitle: Algorithms for Accelerating the Co-simulation of Maxwell's and Drift-Diffusion Equations for Transient Device Simulations in the THz Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we present fast algorithms to accelerate the co-simulation of Maxwell's equations and Drift-Diffusion equations in time domain for device simulations at THz frequencies. The space discretization of both equations is performed in a consistent way using divergence and gradient operators directly obtained from mesh information. The time marching scheme is devised such that there is no need to solve a time-dependent matrix at each time step. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed fast algorithms are demonstrated by comparisons with experimentally verified device simulation results and state-of-the-art transient device simulations.

articleTitle: Simulating Advanced Driver Assistance Systems Using a High-Fidelity Physics-Based Asymptotic Shooting and Bouncing Ray-Tracing Electromagnetics Solver
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Autonomy and electrification have emerged as key drivers of innovation and growth in the automotive industry in recent years. Various advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) have been developed as OEMs race towards a fully autonomous and zero-emissions future. Radar-based ADAS such as adaptive cruise control (ACC), automatic emergency braking (AEB), blind spot detection (BSD), among others are currently being implemented in today's vehicle. Connectivity related ADAS such as vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) using designated short-range communication (DSRC) and ultrawideband (UWB) technologies are poised to become ubiquitous in coming years. Before advanced driver assistance systems are deployed, they need to go through rigorous testing and validation. While measurement is valuable, simulation has emerged as a practical, cost effective and safer approach to testing the robustness of these systems, especially in corner cases.

articleTitle: Measurement and Characterization of an UWB mm Wave 2–40 GHz TCDA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel UWB Tightly-Coupled Dipole Array that operates from the microwave to the mm-Wave regime. A new hybrid fabrication approach that combines 3D printing with PCB technologies and enables real-ization at mm- Wave frequencies is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Simulations of an infinite array are performed and the performance is validated through the measurements of a 20×15 prototype.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of a Patch Antenna using Wideband Modified Split Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Metamaterials are a popular choice to increase the gain of microstrip (patch) antennas, but their transmissivity is notably constrained to ≤ 100 MHz bandwidth in the super high frequency (SHF) band. Sub-classes of metamaterials, including superstrates, multi-resonance rings, and frequency-selective surfaces, enhance the gain of a wideband rectangular patch antenna (RPA), but only at the resonance frequency. We propose a 1 GHz modified split ring resonator (MSRR) that expands the bandwidth gain enhancement range without increasing the size of the overall antenna structure. The study investigates the impact of altering MSRR dimensions and how they affect the magnetic field and the induced current over a wide bandwidth. The MSRR's impedance bandwidth is optimized to be three times broader than conventional SRR, resulting in a peak gain improvement of 5 dBi when placed on top of a wideband RPA.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Multi-Beam Metasurface Antennas for Spaceborne Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Multi-beam antennas are essential in the deployment of high-resolution space imaging systems and high-data-rate satellite communication systems. As the industry transitions to more compact and smaller space platforms, traditional spaceborne multi-beam antennas, such as reflectors and active phased arrays, become impractical due to considerations of size and energy consumption. Consequently, multi-beam metasurface antennas, with their subwavelength profiles and low-power consumption, have begun to attract interest from space agencies and industry. Compared to traditional antennas, metasurface antennas offer more degrees of freedom, enabling extreme beamforming, polarization control, and multiband operation.

articleTitle: Wireless Monitoring of S-Parameters Measurement Using a Nano-VNA for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Measurement of biological metabolites, such as glucose and lactate are important in both healthcare and athletic settings. Many approaches for noninvasive remote sensing of glucose or lactate use on-body resonator circuits that measure changes in resonant frequency to determine concentrations. However, conventional VNAs are impractical for taking on-body measurements as they have to be small and portable so they can measure while the subject is moving. This paper presents an approach that uses “nano” VNAs, non-invasive sensors, and wireless communication circuits to create practical on-body measurement systems capable of transmitting S-parameters data for remote analysis.

articleTitle: On the Suitability of the Julia Programming Language for Computational Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This talk will describe some of the reasons that the Julia programming language (https://ju-lialang.org) is an excellent choice for developing computational electromagnetics codes. Julia is a recently developed, free and open-source computer programming language, primarily intended for high-performance technical computing. A modern, dynamic, high-level language, Julia was specifically created to address identified shortcomings of existing languages used for scientific computing. Although Julia can be used interactively where it “feels” like an interpreted language, it transparently compiles code to machine language prior to execution (JIT compilation), resulting in execution speed competitive with Fortran or C. Indeed, in 2017 Julia joined C, C++, and Fortran as the only languages to have achieved petaflop performance (Regier, Jeffrey, et al., J. Par. Distrib. Comput. 127 (2019): 89–104).

articleTitle: Wideband Dual-Polarized Log-Periodic Pyramid Antenna at VHF /UHF
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A wideband dual-polarized log-periodic pyramid antenna design is investigated for applications at VHF /UHF, consisting of four log-periodic trapezoid wire dipole faces. Simulations were done in FEKO and measurements were conducted with a foam-supported prototype. This paper describes the antenna design, electromagnetic simulations and anechoic chamber measurements of the antenna. Good agreement between simulations and measurements of the reflection coefficient and boresight realized gain is demonstrated over wide bandwidth.
